An equivalence class $[\gamma]$ is a **tangent vector** at $p$, and the set of all of them is $T_pM$; via $[\gamma] \mapsto (\varphi \circ \gamma)'(0)$ it corresponds bijectively to $\mathbb{R}^n$, and transporting addition and scalar multiplication makes it an $n$-dimensional real vector space (the coordinate change is linear, so the structure does not depend on the chart). Geometrically, $[\gamma]$ is the **velocity vector** of the curve at $p$.

**(b) Derivations.** Let $C^\infty(M)$ be the smooth functions on $M$. A **derivation** at $p$ is a linear map $v: C^\infty(M) \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the **Leibniz rule** $v(fg) = f(p)\,v(g) + g(p)\,v(f)$; these form the vector space $\mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$. The two notions correspond through $[\gamma] \mapsto \bigl(f \mapsto (f \circ \gamma)'(0)\bigr)$: the product rule shows the right-hand side is a derivation, the chain rule shows chart-independence, and conversely every derivation is a directional derivative in any chart. The correspondence is a **linear isomorphism**, so one freely switches between the geometric picture (curves) and the algebraic one (derivations).

Fix a chart $(U,\varphi)$ and write $x^i = u^i \circ \varphi$ for the coordinate functions. The basis vectors $\partial/\partial x^i\big|_p$ are the derivations $f \mapsto \frac{\partial (f \circ \varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)$. Every $v \in T_pM$ has the unique expansion $v = \sum_{i=1}^n v^i\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\big|_p$ with $v^i = v(x^i)$; in particular $\dim T_pM = n = \dim M$.

For a smooth map $f: M \to N$, the **differential** (pushforward) $df_p: T_pM \to T_{f(p)}N$ is defined by $df_p[\gamma] = [f \circ \gamma]$ in terms of curves, or by $(df_p(v))(g) = v(g \circ f)$ for $g \in C^\infty(N)$ in terms of derivations. It is linear and respects composition (chain rule): $d(g \circ f)_p = dg_{f(p)} \circ df_p$. In coordinates $x^i$ near $p$ and $y^j$ near $f(p)$, with $y^j = f^j(x)$, its matrix in the corresponding bases is exactly the **Jacobian matrix** $\bigl(\partial f^j/\partial x^i(p)\bigr)$. If $f$ is a diffeomorphism, $df_p$ is invertible with $(df_p)^{-1} = d(f^{-1})_{f(p)}$.
derivation: 固定 $p\in M$。考虑光滑曲线 $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to M$，$\gamma(0)=p$。取含 $p$ 的图 $(U,\varphi)$，规定 $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2\iff(\varphi\circ\gamma_1)'(0)=(\varphi\circ\gamma_2)'(0)$。换图 $\psi$ 时，链式法则给出 $$\begin{aligned}(\psi\circ\gamma)'(0)&=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\\&\quad\cdot\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr].\end{aligned}$$ 右端是固定线性映射作用在速度上，故在一个图中相等蕴含在另一个图中相等；又 $\sim$ 显然是等价关系。于是等价类 $[\gamma]$ 与图无关，定义为 $p$ 处的切向量，全体记 $T_pM$。

用图把 $T_pM$ 与 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 对齐：$\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)$。由第 1 步它是双射。定义 $$\begin{aligned}\,[\gamma_1]+[\gamma_2]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_1]+\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_2]\bigr),\\ c\,[\gamma]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(c\,\Theta_\varphi[\gamma]\bigr).\end{aligned}$$ 需检验与图无关：换图后 $\Theta_\psi\circ\Theta_\varphi^{-1}=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})(\varphi(p))$ 是线性同构，线性运算在可逆线性映射下保持，故所得向量空间结构与图无关。结论：$T_pM$ 是 $n$ 维实向量空间，零向量是常值曲线的类；几何上 $[\gamma]$ 就是曲线在 $p$ 的速度。

另一条路线：称线性映射 $v:C^\infty(M)\to\mathbb{R}$ 为 $p$ 处的导子，若满足莱布尼茨法则 $v(fg)=f(p)v(g)+g(p)v(f)$。由 $[\gamma]\mapsto\bigl(f\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr)$ 得到导子：线性显然，乘积法则给出莱布尼茨。反之设 $v$ 是导子。先用截断函数可证 $v(f)$ 只依赖 $f$ 在 $p$ 附近的值，故可在局部讨论。取图并以 $x^i$ 记坐标函数（必要时用截断函数把 $x^i$ 延拓到整个 $M$，这不改变 $p$ 附近的取值），对 $f$ 用带积分余项的泰勒公式，在 $p$ 的邻域内 $$\begin{aligned}f&=f(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i g_i,\\ g_i(p)&=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\Big|_{\varphi(p)}.\end{aligned}$$ 由 $v(\text{常数})=0$ 与 $x^i(p)=0$，莱布尼茨法则给出 $$v(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i(p)v(g_i)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p),$$ 故 $v$ 由数组 $(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$ 完全决定。取曲线使 $\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$，即得 $v=v_\gamma$。结论：$T_pM\cong\mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$ 为线性同构。

取图 $(U,\varphi)$，坐标函数 $x^i=u^i\circ\varphi$。定义 $$\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p(f):=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr).$$ 由第 3 步的公式，每个 $v\in T_pM$ 可唯一写成 $$v=\sum_{i=1}^n v^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,\qquad v^i=v(x^i)=dx^i(v),$$ 故这 $n$ 个向量构成基，$\dim T_pM=n$。换图 $y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$ 时链式法则给出 $$\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_p=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}\bigl(\psi(p)\bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,$$ 即切向量的坐标按 $v^i=\sum_j\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}w^j$ 变换（反变），变换矩阵可逆。

设 $F:M\to N$ 光滑。定义 $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ 为 $dF_p[\gamma]:=[F\circ\gamma]$。良定义：若 $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2$，取 $p$、$F(p)$ 附近的图，$F$ 的坐标表示 $\tilde F=\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}$ 光滑，则 $$(\psi\circ F\circ\gamma_i)'(0)=D\tilde F\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma_i)'(0)\bigr],$$ 两个速度相等故像速度相等。$dF_p$ 线性（坐标中就是乘固定矩阵），且 $$d(G\circ F)_p=dG_{F(p)}\circ dF_p,\qquad d(\mathrm{id}_M)_p=\mathrm{id}.$$ 用导子写就是 $(dF_p v)(g)=v(g\circ F)$，$g\in C^\infty(N)$。结论：切映射把 $M$ 的切方向推到 $N$，复合对应矩阵相乘。

在基下写出矩阵：设 $y^j=F^j(x)$，则 $$dF_p\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}(p)\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_{F(p)},$$ 即 $dF_p$ 的矩阵是雅可比矩阵 $(\partial F^j/\partial x^i)$，故 $\operatorname{rank}dF_p$ 与图无关。若 $\dim M=\dim N=n$ 且 $dF_p$ 可逆，则由反函数定理 $F$ 在 $p$ 附近是微分同胚，且 $(dF_p)^{-1}=d(F^{-1})_{F(p)}$。例：$S^2=F^{-1}(1)$，$F(x)=|x|^2$，$dF_p=2p^{\mathsf T}\ne0$，由正则水平集定理，$T_pS^2=\ker dF_p=\{v:v\cdot p=0\}=p^\perp$。注意方向：切映射只把 $T_pM$ 送到 $T_{F(p)}N$；当 $F$ 不是单射时，向量场一般不能整体推前，而形式总可以拉回。
derivationEn: Fix $p\in M$ and consider smooth curves $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=p$. Relative to a chart $(U,\varphi)$ around $p$, declare $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2\iff(\varphi\circ\gamma_1)'(0)=(\varphi\circ\gamma_2)'(0)$. For another chart $\psi$, the chain rule gives $$\begin{aligned}(\psi\circ\gamma)'(0)&=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\\&\quad\cdot\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr].\end{aligned}$$ where a fixed linear map acts on the velocity, so equality in one chart implies equality in the other; and $\sim$ is plainly an equivalence relation. Hence the class $[\gamma]$ is chart-independent; it is called a tangent vector at $p$, and the set of all classes is $T_pM$.

Use a chart to identify $T_pM$ with $\mathbb{R}^n$: $\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(\varphi\circ\gamma)'(0)$, a bijection by Step 1. Set $$\begin{aligned}\,[\gamma_1]+[\gamma_2]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_1]+\Theta_\varphi[\gamma_2]\bigr),\\ c\,[\gamma]&:=\Theta_\varphi^{-1}\bigl(c\,\Theta_\varphi[\gamma]\bigr).\end{aligned}$$ This is chart-independent: after a change of chart $\Theta_\psi\circ\Theta_\varphi^{-1}=D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})(\varphi(p))$ is a linear isomorphism, and linear operations are preserved under invertible linear maps, so the vector-space structure does not depend on the chart. Hence $T_pM$ is an $n$-dimensional real vector space, its zero vector being the class of a constant curve; geometrically $[\gamma]$ is the velocity of the curve at $p$.

Alternative route: a linear map $v:C^\infty(M)\to\mathbb{R}$ is a derivation at $p$ if it satisfies the Leibniz rule $v(fg)=f(p)v(g)+g(p)v(f)$. The map $[\gamma]\mapsto\bigl(f\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(0)\bigr)$ produces derivations: linearity is clear and the product rule gives Leibniz. Conversely, let $v$ be a derivation. A cutoff-function argument shows that $v(f)$ depends only on $f$ near $p$, so the discussion may be local. Take a chart with coordinate functions $x^i$ (extend them over $M$ by cutoff functions if necessary; this does not change their values near $p$) and apply Taylor's formula with integral remainder near $p$: $$\begin{aligned}f&=f(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i g_i,\\ g_i(p)&=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\Big|_{\varphi(p)}.\end{aligned}$$ Since $v(\text{constant})=0$ and $x^i(p)=0$, the Leibniz rule gives $$v(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p)+\sum_{i=1}^n x^i(p)v(g_i)=\sum_{i=1}^n v(x^i)g_i(p),$$ so $v$ is determined by the array $(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$. Choosing a curve with $\Theta_\varphi([\gamma])=(v(x^1),\dots,v(x^n))$ gives $v=v_\gamma$. Hence $T_pM\cong\mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$ linearly.

Take a chart $(U,\varphi)$ with coordinate functions $x^i=u^i\circ\varphi$ and define $$\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p(f):=\frac{\partial(f\circ\varphi^{-1})}{\partial u^i}\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr).$$ By the formula of Step 3 every $v\in T_pM$ has a unique expansion $$v=\sum_{i=1}^n v^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,\qquad v^i=v(x^i)=dx^i(v),$$ so these $n$ vectors form a basis and $\dim T_pM=n$. Under a change of chart $y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$ the chain rule gives $$\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_p=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}\bigl(\psi(p)\bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,$$ so tangent coordinates transform by $v^i=\sum_j\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^j}w^j$ (contravariantly), with an invertible transition matrix.

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth. Define $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ by $dF_p[\gamma]:=[F\circ\gamma]$. It is well defined: if $\gamma_1\sim\gamma_2$, choose charts near $p$ and $F(p)$; the coordinate expression $\tilde F=\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}$ is smooth, so $$(\psi\circ F\circ\gamma_i)'(0)=D\tilde F\bigl(\varphi(p)\bigr)\bigl[(\varphi\circ\gamma_i)'(0)\bigr],$$ and equal velocities give equal image velocities. The map $dF_p$ is linear (in coordinates it is multiplication by a fixed matrix), and $$d(G\circ F)_p=dG_{F(p)}\circ dF_p,\qquad d(\mathrm{id}_M)_p=\mathrm{id}.$$ In derivation form $(dF_p v)(g)=v(g\circ F)$ for $g\in C^\infty(N)$. Thus the differential pushes tangent directions from $M$ to $N$, and composition corresponds to multiplication of matrices.

In bases the matrix is transparent: if $y^j=F^j(x)$, then $$dF_p\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}(p)\frac{\partial}{\partial y^j}\Big|_{F(p)},$$ so the matrix of $dF_p$ is the Jacobian $(\partial F^j/\partial x^i)$ and $\operatorname{rank}dF_p$ is chart-independent. If $\dim M=\dim N=n$ and $dF_p$ is invertible, the inverse function theorem makes $F$ a local diffeomorphism near $p$, with $(dF_p)^{-1}=d(F^{-1})_{F(p)}$. Example: $S^2=F^{-1}(1)$ for $F(x)=|x|^2$ has $dF_p=2p^{\mathsf T}\ne0$, so by the regular level set theorem $T_pS^2=\ker dF_p=\{v:v\cdot p=0\}=p^\perp$. Mind the direction: the differential only maps $T_pM$ to $T_{F(p)}N$; when $F$ is not injective a vector field generally cannot be pushed forward globally, whereas forms can always be pulled back.

formulas.note: 曲线定义：两条过 $p$ 的曲线等价当且仅当在任一张图中它们的坐标表示在 $0$ 处有相同的导数；判别与图的选择无关。
formulas.noteEn: The curve definition: two curves through $p$ are equivalent exactly when their coordinate expressions have the same derivative at $0$; the test is independent of the chart.

formulas.note: 导子定义：切向量就是作用在光滑函数上、满足莱布尼茨法则的线性映射；$v(f)$ 只依赖 $f$ 在 $p$ 附近的值。
formulas.noteEn: The derivation definition: a tangent vector is a linear functional on smooth functions satisfying the Leibniz rule; $v(f)$ depends only on $f$ near $p$.

formulas.note: 两种定义的等价（且是线性同构）：曲线的等价类与导子一一对应，对应的显式公式就是沿曲线求方向导数。
formulas.noteEn: Equivalence of the two definitions (a linear isomorphism): classes of curves correspond one-to-one with derivations, explicitly by differentiating functions along the curve.

formulas.latex: v = \sum_{i=1}^{n} v^i \frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Big|_p,\qquad v^i = v(x^i),\qquad \dim T_pM = n
formulas.note: 局部坐标下的标准写法：$\{\partial/\partial x^i|_p\}$ 是一组基，第 $i$ 个系数等于 $v$ 作用在第 $i$ 个坐标函数上；切空间维数等于流形维数。
formulas.noteEn: The standard local form: the vectors $\partial/\partial x^i|_p$ form a basis, the $i$-th coefficient is $v$ applied to the $i$-th coordinate function, and $\dim T_pM = \dim M$.

formulas.latex: df_p\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\Bigr) = \sum_j \frac{\partial f^j}{\partial x^i}(p)\, \frac{\partial}{\partial y^j},\qquad d(g \circ f)_p = dg_{f(p)} \circ df_p
formulas.note: 切映射的矩阵就是雅可比矩阵；复合的切映射满足链式法则（矩阵相乘）。$f$ 为微分同胚时 $df_p$ 是线性同构。
formulas.noteEn: The matrix of the differential is the Jacobian matrix, and composition of maps corresponds to multiplication of Jacobians (chain rule). If $f$ is a diffeomorphism, $df_p$ is a linear isomorphism.

properties: 两种定义等价：$[\gamma] \mapsto \bigl(f \mapsto (f \circ \gamma)'(0)\bigr)$ 是 $T_pM \to \mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$ 的线性同构；几何直觉（速度）与代数操作（求导）可以自由切换
$\dim T_pM = \dim M = n$；$T_pM$ 只依赖 $M$ 在 $p$ 附近的结构，$p$ 的任意开邻域在同一点的切空间与全流形相同
切向量是局部对象：$v(f)$ 只依赖 $f$ 在 $p$ 的某邻域内的值（用截断函数可证）
切映射 $df_p$ 线性、与复合相容（链式法则），$d(\mathrm{id}_M)_p = \mathrm{id}$；微分同胚的切映射是线性同构；反函数定理：$\dim M = \dim N$ 且 $df_p$ 处处可逆时 $f$ 是局部微分同胚
嵌入 $\mathbb{R}^N$ 中的流形：$T_pM$ 由过 $p$ 的曲线速度向量组成；若 $M = F^{-1}(c)$ 是正则水平集，则 $T_pM = \ker dF_p$，例如 $T_pS^n = \{v \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}: v \cdot p = 0\}$
propertiesEn: The two definitions agree: $[\gamma] \mapsto \bigl(f \mapsto (f \circ \gamma)'(0)\bigr)$ is a linear isomorphism $T_pM \to \mathrm{Der}_p(C^\infty(M))$, so geometric intuition (velocities) and algebra (differentiation) are interchangeable
$\dim T_pM = \dim M = n$; $T_pM$ depends only on the structure of $M$ near $p$, and any open neighbourhood of $p$ has the same tangent space at $p$
Tangent vectors are local objects: $v(f)$ depends only on the values of $f$ in a neighbourhood of $p$ (provable with cutoff functions)

The differential $df_p$ is linear and respects composition (chain rule), $d(\mathrm{id}_M)_p = \mathrm{id}$; diffeomorphisms have invertible differentials; conversely the inverse function theorem: if $\dim M = \dim N$ and $df_p$ is invertible everywhere, $f$ is a local diffeomorphism

For embedded manifolds: $T_pM$ consists of velocities of curves through $p$; if $M = F^{-1}(c)$ is a regular level set then $T_pM = \ker dF_p$, e.g. $T_pS^n = \{v \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}: v \cdot p = 0\}$

examples.problem: 设 $S^2 = \{(x,y,z): x^2+y^2+z^2 = 1\}$，$p = (0,0,1)$ 为北极，$\gamma(t) = (\sin t, 0, \cos t)$。求 $T_pS^2$，并用球极投影图求 $[\gamma]$ 在基 $\{\partial/\partial u, \partial/\partial v\}$ 下的坐标。
examples.solution:
(i) 由正则水平集求切空间：$S^2 = F^{-1}(1)$，$F(x,y,z) = x^2+y^2+z^2$，$dF_p = (2x,2y,2z)\big|_p = (0,0,2) \neq 0$，故 $p$ 是正则点，$T_pS^2 = \ker dF_p = \{(v_1,v_2,v_3): 2v_3 = 0\} = \{v_3 = 0\} = \mathrm{span}\{\partial/\partial x|_p,\ \partial/\partial y|_p\}$（把 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 的坐标用作环境坐标）。等价地 $T_pS^2 = \{v: v \cdot p = 0\} = p^{\perp}$。

(ii) 取南极球极投影图 $\sigma_S(x,y,z) = \bigl(\frac{x}{1+z},\ \frac{y}{1+z}\bigr)$，坐标记 $(u,v)$。曲线变为 $u(t) = \frac{\sin t}{1+\cos t} = \tan\frac{t}{2}$，$v(t) = 0$，故 $(\sigma_S \circ \gamma)'(0) = \bigl(\frac{1}{2}, 0\bigr)$，即 $[\gamma] = \frac{1}{2}\,\frac{\partial}{\partial u}\big|_p$。

(iii) 一致性检查：$\sigma_S^{-1}(u,v) = \frac{(2u,\ 2v,\ 1-u^2-v^2)}{1+u^2+v^2}$，在 $p$（即 $(u,v) = (0,0)$）处 $d\sigma_S^{-1}\bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial u}\bigr) = (2,0,0)$（对 $u$ 求偏导后在原点取值）。于是 $\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial u} \mapsto (1,0,0)$，恰好等于 $\gamma'(0)$；同时 $(1,0,0) \cdot p = 0$，与 (i) 的 $v \cdot p = 0$ 相符。

examples.problem: 设 $f: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$，$f(x,y) = (x^2-y^2,\ 2xy)$。求 $f$ 在 $p = (1,1)$ 处的切映射 $df_p$ 的雅可比矩阵，计算 $df_p(1,0)$ 与 $df_p(0,1)$，并用链式法则验证曲线 $\gamma(t) = (1+t,\ 1)$ 的像的导数。
examples.solution:
雅可比矩阵：$J_f(x,y) = \begin{pmatrix} 2x & -2y \\ 2y & 2x \end{pmatrix}$，在 $p=(1,1)$ 处 $M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$。故 $df_p(1,0) = (2,2)$，$df_p(0,1) = (-2,2)$。

复数对照：把 $(x,y)$ 看成 $z = x+iy$，则 $f$ 就是 $z \mapsto z^2$，而切映射就是「乘以 $f'(z) = 2z$」。在 $z = 1+i$ 处 $2z = 2+2i$：乘以 $1$ 得 $(2,2)$，乘以 $i$ 得 $(2+2i)i = -2+2i$，与上面一致。

链式法则验证：$f(\gamma(t)) = ((1+t)^2-1,\ 2(1+t)) = (2t+t^2,\ 2+2t)$，故 $\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0} f(\gamma(t)) = (2,2)$；而 $df_p(\gamma'(0)) = df_p(1,0) = (2,2)$，两者相符——这正是 $d(f \circ \gamma)_0 = df_p \circ d\gamma_0$。

expression.text: df_p : T_pM → T_{f(p)}N，坐标下矩阵为雅可比矩阵 (∂f^j/∂x^i)
expression.note: 切映射是 f 在 p 处的最佳线性逼近；它把曲线（速度向量）映成曲线（速度向量）。

manifold-vector-fields.definition:
**向量场**是把每点 $p$ 映到切空间里一个向量 $X_p \in T_pM$ 的规则 $X: M \to TM$，并要求它「光滑地依赖 $p$」。光滑性有两种等价说法：在一张张图里 $X$ 的系数是光滑函数；或者，$X$ 作为作用在函数上的算子把每个 $f \in C^\infty(M)$ 映到光滑函数 $X(f)$。**关键对应**：光滑向量场与 $C^\infty(M)$ 上的**导子**（一阶微分算子）一一对应——$X$ 是实线性的，且满足莱布尼茨法则 $X(fg) = f\,X(g) + g\,X(f)$；反之，每个满足这两条的算子都来自唯一的向量场。于是在局部坐标下 $X = \sum_i X^i(x)\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}$，其中系数 $X^i$ 光滑，而 $X(f)$ 处处等于 $f$ 沿 $X$ 的逐点方向导数。可以说：**向量场 = 对函数求方向导数的一阶微分算子**。

给定向量场 $X$，**积分曲线**是满足 $\gamma'(t) = X(\gamma(t))$ 的曲线；在局部坐标里这就是一阶常微分方程组 $\dot x^i = X^i(x)$。由 **ODE 的局部存在唯一性定理**（Picard–Lindelöf），过每一点存在唯一一条极大积分曲线，并且在不同图里得到的局部解自动一致，可以整体拼接。把「从 $p$ 出发沿 $X$ 走 $t$ 时间」记为 $\varphi_t(p)$，就得到**局部流**：$\varphi_0(p) = p$ 且 $\frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(p) = X(\varphi_t(p))$。由唯一性还得到**半群性质** $\varphi_{s+t} = \varphi_s \circ \varphi_t$（两边都有定义时），以及每个 $\varphi_t$ 是局部微分同胚（逆为 $\varphi_{-t}$）。过不同点的极大积分曲线要么重合、要么像集不交；这正是「一个人不能同时走在两条轨道上」。

若 $X$ 的流对**一切** $t \in \mathbb{R}$ 都有定义，就称 $X$ **完备**；此时 $\varphi: \mathbb{R} \times M \to M$ 光滑，$\{\varphi_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ 是 $M$ 的单参数微分同胚群。**紧流形上任何光滑向量场都完备**：紧性给出局部存在时间的一致下界，有限步拼接即可把流延拓到任意大的 $|t|$；而非紧流形上可以不完备——$\mathbb{R}$ 上的 $X = x^2\,\partial/\partial x$ 的积分曲线 $x(t) = \frac{x_0}{1 - x_0 t}$（$x_0 > 0$）在 $t \to 1/x_0$ 时发散。**奇点**（平衡点）是满足 $X(p) = 0$ 的点：此时常值曲线 $\gamma(t) \equiv p$ 是一条积分曲线，由唯一性它对一切 $t$ 成立——奇点恰是流的不动点。

几何上，向量场是流形上的速度场，流是「随流体运动」的映射；研究向量场及其流的定性行为（奇点、周期轨道、稳定性）就是流形上的动力系统。全体光滑向量场记作 $\mathfrak{X}(M)$，它既是 $C^\infty(M)$-模，又在李括号 $[X,Y]$ 下构成无穷维李代数：$[X,Y] = 0$ 当且仅当两个流局部交换，这为李导数与对称性研究提供了语言。
manifold-vector-fields.definitionEn:
A **vector field** assigns to every point $p$ a tangent vector $X_p \in T_pM$ via a rule $X: M \to TM$ that depends smoothly on $p$. Smoothness has two equivalent formulations: the coefficients of $X$ are smooth in every chart; equivalently, $X$ acts on functions and sends each $f \in C^\infty(M)$ to a smooth function $X(f)$. **Key correspondence**: smooth vector fields are in one-to-one correspondence with **derivations** of $C^\infty(M)$ (first-order differential operators)—$X$ is real-linear and satisfies the Leibniz rule $X(fg) = f\,X(g) + g\,X(f)$, and conversely every operator with these two properties comes from a unique vector field. In local coordinates $X = \sum_i X^i(x)\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}$ with smooth coefficients, and $X(f)$ is the pointwise directional derivative of $f$ along $X$.

Given $X$, an **integral curve** is a curve with $\gamma'(t) = X(\gamma(t))$; in local coordinates this is the first-order ODE system $\dot x^i = X^i(x)$. The **local existence and uniqueness theorem for ODEs** (Picard–Lindelöf) yields, through each point, a unique maximal integral curve, and the local solutions obtained in different charts agree, so they glue globally. Writing $\varphi_t(p)$ for "starting at $p$ and following $X$ for time $t$" gives the **local flow**: $\varphi_0(p) = p$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(p) = X(\varphi_t(p))$. Uniqueness also gives the **semigroup property** $\varphi_{s+t} = \varphi_s \circ \varphi_t$ (whenever both sides are defined), and each $\varphi_t$ is a local diffeomorphism with inverse $\varphi_{-t}$. Maximal integral curves through different points either coincide or have disjoint images.

If the flow of $X$ is defined for **all** $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the field is called **complete**; then $\varphi: \mathbb{R} \times M \to M$ is smooth and $\{\varphi_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ is a one-parameter group of diffeomorphisms of $M$. **Every smooth vector field on a compact manifold is complete**: compactness gives a uniform lower bound on the local existence time, and finitely many steps extend the flow to arbitrarily large $|t|$. On non-compact manifolds completeness can fail: for $X = x^2\,\partial/\partial x$ on $\mathbb{R}$ the integral curve $x(t) = \frac{x_0}{1 - x_0 t}$ (for $x_0 > 0$) blows up as $t \to 1/x_0$. A **singularity** (equilibrium) is a point with $X(p) = 0$: the constant curve $\gamma(t) \equiv p$ is then an integral curve, and by uniqueness it persists for all $t$—singularities are exactly the fixed points of the flow.

Geometrically, a vector field is a velocity field on the manifold and its flow describes motion with the fluid; the qualitative study of vector fields and their flows (singularities, periodic orbits, stability) is dynamical systems on manifolds. The space $\mathfrak{X}(M)$ of all smooth vector fields is a $C^\infty(M)$-module and an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra under the Lie bracket $[X,Y]$: $[X,Y] = 0$ if and only if the two flows commute locally, which is the language of Lie derivatives and symmetry.
derivation: 向量场是光滑截面 $X:M\to TM$，即 $\pi\circ X=\mathrm{id}_M$，且在每张图里 $$X=\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i},\qquad X^i\in C^\infty(U).$$ 等价地，$X$ 作用在函数上：$X(f)=df(X)$，它是实线性且满足莱布尼茨法则 $X(fg)=fX(g)+gX(f)$ 的算子；反之这样的导子必为上述形式，因为由泰勒公式它在坐标中是二阶导为零的一阶算子。全体光滑向量场记 $\mathfrak{X}(M)$，它是 $C^\infty(M)$-模：$(fX)(g)=fX(g)$。结论：向量场就是对函数求方向导数的一阶微分算子，光滑性就是系数光滑。

给定 $X$，积分曲线是光滑 $\gamma:I\to M$ 满足 $$\gamma'(t)=X\bigl(\gamma(t)\bigr),$$ 在图中即一阶方程组 $\dot x^i=X^i(x(t))$。因 $X^i$ 光滑（从而局部 Lipschitz），Picard–Lindelöf 定理给出：对每点 $p$ 存在 $\varepsilon_p>0$ 与唯一的解 $\gamma_p:(-\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_p)\to M$，$\gamma_p(0)=p$；不同图上的局部解在重叠区一致，故可拼接成唯一的极大积分曲线，其定义区间 $I_p$ 是含 $0$ 的开区间。唯一性还给出：两条极大积分曲线若在某一时刻同处一点，则整条重合；否则像集不交。于是极大积分曲线把 $M$ 分成互不相交的轨道。

令 $\varphi_t(p):=\gamma_p(t)$，定义域 $D=\{(t,p):t\in I_p\}$。由 ODE 解对初值的光滑依赖性，$D$ 是开集且 $\varphi:D\to M$ 光滑。基本性质：$$\varphi_0=\mathrm{id}_M,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(p)=X\bigl(\varphi_t(p)\bigr).$$ 半群性质：固定 $p$ 与 $s$，曲线 $t\mapsto\varphi_{s+t}(p)$ 与 $t\mapsto\varphi_s(\varphi_t(p))$ 都解同一 ODE，且在 $t=0$ 都等于 $\varphi_s(p)$，由唯一性二者在公共定义域上相等：$\varphi_{s+t}=\varphi_s\circ\varphi_t$。取 $s=-t$ 得 $\varphi_t\circ\varphi_{-t}=\mathrm{id}$，故每个 $\varphi_t$ 是局部微分同胚，逆为 $\varphi_{-t}$。若 $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$，称 $X$ 完备，此时 $\{\varphi_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ 是单参数微分同胚群。

李括号定义为导子的交换子：$$[X,Y](f):=X\bigl(Y(f)\bigr)-Y\bigl(X(f)\bigr).$$ 它仍是导子：把 $XY(fg)$ 与 $YX(fg)$ 展开，含 $X(f)Y(g)$ 与 $Y(f)X(g)$ 的交叉项相消，剩下 $f[X,Y](g)+g[X,Y](f)$。在坐标中 $$\begin{aligned}&[X,Y]=\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial Y^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\\&\quad-\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n Y^i\frac{\partial X^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}.\end{aligned}$$ 推导：两边都是导子，只需比较作用在坐标函数 $x^k$ 上的值，链式法则即得上式。由定义立即有反称性 $[X,Y]=-[Y,X]$ 与雅可比恒等式 $$[[X,Y],Z]+[[Y,Z],X]+[[Z,X],Y]=0,$$ 后者展开后每项出现两次、符号相反。结论：$\mathfrak{X}(M)$ 是无穷维李代数。注意 $[fX,gY]=fg[X,Y]+f(Xg)Y-g(Yf)X$，故括号不是 $C^\infty(M)$-双线性的，它不是张量。

括号的几何意义是流的非交换性。设 $X,Y$ 的流分别为 $\varphi^X,\varphi^Y$，$p\in M$，$t$ 充分小使所有复合有定义。在图中把每个流按 $t$ 展开：$$\varphi^X_t(x)=x+tX(x)+\frac{t^2}{2}DX(x)\bigl[X(x)\bigr]+O(t^3),$$ 对 $Y$ 同理。把 $$\varphi^Y_{-t}\circ\varphi^X_{-t}\circ\varphi^Y_t\circ\varphi^X_t(p)$$ 逐次代入并按 $t$ 的幂整理：$O(t)$ 项抵消，$O(t^2)$ 中的 $\frac12DXX+\frac12DYY$ 也成对抵消，只剩 $$p+t^2\bigl(DY\cdot X-DX\cdot Y\bigr)(p)+O(t^3)=p+t^2[X,Y]_p+O(t^3).$$ 因此 $[X,Y]$ 是「先沿 $X$、再沿 $Y$ 各走 $t$，再依次退回」所得位移的二阶主部。特别地，$[X,Y]=0$ 时 $(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=Y$（因 $\frac{d}{dt}(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=(\varphi^X_t)_*[X,Y]=0$），故 $\varphi^X_t\circ\varphi^Y_s\circ\varphi^X_{-t}$ 与 $\varphi^Y_s$ 是同一向量场的流且初值相同，两流局部交换；反之若两流交换，由上面的展开得 $[X,Y]=0$。条件：$X,Y$ 至少 $C^2$，且 $t$ 足够小。

完备性。若 $M$ 紧且 $X$ 光滑，则存在 $\varepsilon>0$，使对任意 $p$ 积分曲线都在 $|t|<\varepsilon$ 上有定义：每点有邻域 $U_p$ 与时间 $\delta_p$，取有限子覆盖并用 Lebesgue 数即可让「起点在同一邻域内」的解有统一存在时间。于是对任意 $T$，用 $\lceil|T|/\varepsilon\rceil$ 步拼接即可定义 $\varphi_T$，唯一性保证拼接一致，故 $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$：紧流形上向量场必完备。非紧时可能失败：$X=x^2\partial_x$ 在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上的积分曲线为 $$x(t)=\frac{x_0}{1-x_0t}\quad(x_0>0),$$ 在 $t\to1/x_0$ 时爆破，无法延拓。奇点 $X(p)=0$ 处常值曲线是积分曲线，由唯一性 $\varphi_t(p)=p$ 对一切 $t$ 成立；反之若 $\varphi_t(p)=p$ 对一切 $t$ 成立，对 $t$ 在 $0$ 处求导得 $X(p)=0$。
derivationEn: A vector field is a smooth section $X:M\to TM$, i.e. $\pi\circ X=\mathrm{id}_M$, and in every chart $$X=\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i},\qquad X^i\in C^\infty(U).$$ Equivalently $X$ acts on functions by $X(f)=df(X)$: a real-linear operator satisfying the Leibniz rule $X(fg)=fX(g)+gX(f)$. Conversely every such derivation has the displayed form, because Taylor's formula shows that in coordinates it is a first-order operator with no second derivatives. The smooth vector fields form $\mathfrak{X}(M)$, a $C^\infty(M)$-module under $(fX)(g)=fX(g)$. Thus a vector field is a first-order differential operator, and smoothness means smooth coefficients.

Given $X$, an integral curve is a smooth $\gamma:I\to M$ with $$\gamma'(t)=X\bigl(\gamma(t)\bigr),$$ which in a chart is the first-order system $\dot x^i=X^i(x(t))$. Since the $X^i$ are smooth (hence locally Lipschitz), Picard–Lindelöf gives, for each $p$, some $\varepsilon_p>0$ and a unique solution $\gamma_p:(-\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_p)\to M$ with $\gamma_p(0)=p$; local solutions in different charts agree on overlaps, so they glue into a unique maximal integral curve with open interval $I_p\ni0$. Uniqueness also shows that two maximal integral curves which meet at one time coincide entirely, and otherwise have disjoint images. The maximal curves therefore foliate $M$ into disjoint orbits.

Set $\varphi_t(p):=\gamma_p(t)$ on the domain $D=\{(t,p):t\in I_p\}$. Smooth dependence of ODE solutions on initial data makes $D$ open and $\varphi:D\to M$ smooth. The basic properties are $$\varphi_0=\mathrm{id}_M,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(p)=X\bigl(\varphi_t(p)\bigr).$$ Semigroup law: fix $p$ and $s$; both $t\mapsto\varphi_{s+t}(p)$ and $t\mapsto\varphi_s(\varphi_t(p))$ solve the same ODE and agree at $t=0$, namely at $\varphi_s(p)$, so uniqueness gives $\varphi_{s+t}=\varphi_s\circ\varphi_t$ on the common domain. Taking $s=-t$ yields $\varphi_t\circ\varphi_{-t}=\mathrm{id}$, so each $\varphi_t$ is a local diffeomorphism with inverse $\varphi_{-t}$. If $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$, then $X$ is complete and $\{\varphi_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ is a one-parameter group of diffeomorphisms.

The Lie bracket is the commutator of derivations: $$[X,Y](f):=X\bigl(Y(f)\bigr)-Y\bigl(X(f)\bigr).$$ It is again a derivation: expanding $XY(fg)$ and $YX(fg)$, the mixed terms containing $X(f)Y(g)$ and $Y(f)X(g)$ cancel, leaving $f[X,Y](g)+g[X,Y](f)$. In coordinates $$\begin{aligned}&[X,Y]=\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n X^i\frac{\partial Y^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\\&\quad-\sum_{k=1}^n\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n Y^i\frac{\partial X^k}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}.\end{aligned}$$ Indeed both sides are derivations, so it suffices to compare them on the coordinate functions $x^k$, where the chain rule gives the displayed formula. The definition immediately yields antisymmetry $[X,Y]=-[Y,X]$ and the Jacobi identity $$[[X,Y],Z]+[[Y,Z],X]+[[Z,X],Y]=0,$$ since expansion produces each term twice with opposite signs. Hence $\mathfrak{X}(M)$ is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra. Note $[fX,gY]=fg[X,Y]+f(Xg)Y-g(Yf)X$, so the bracket is not $C^\infty(M)$-bilinear and is not a tensor.

Geometrically the bracket measures non-commutativity of flows. Let $\varphi^X,\varphi^Y$ be the flows of $X,Y$ and fix $p\in M$, with $t$ small enough that all composites are defined. In a chart expand each flow in $t$: $$\varphi^X_t(x)=x+tX(x)+\frac{t^2}{2}DX(x)\bigl[X(x)\bigr]+O(t^3),$$ and likewise for $Y$. Substituting successively into $$\varphi^Y_{-t}\circ\varphi^X_{-t}\circ\varphi^Y_t\circ\varphi^X_t(p)$$ and collecting powers of $t$: the $O(t)$ terms cancel, the $\frac12DXX+\frac12DYY$ terms in $O(t^2)$ cancel in pairs, and only $$p+t^2\bigl(DY\cdot X-DX\cdot Y\bigr)(p)+O(t^3)=p+t^2[X,Y]_p+O(t^3)$$ remains. Thus $[X,Y]$ is the second-order principal part of the displacement obtained by going $t$ along $X$, then $t$ along $Y$, then back along both. In particular, if $[X,Y]=0$ then $(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=Y$ (because $\frac{d}{dt}(\varphi^X_t)_*Y=(\varphi^X_t)_*[X,Y]=0$), so $\varphi^X_t\circ\varphi^Y_s\circ\varphi^X_{-t}$ and $\varphi^Y_s$ are flows of the same field with the same initial value and hence coincide, giving local commutation; conversely, commuting flows force $[X,Y]=0$ by the expansion. Hypotheses: $X,Y$ at least $C^2$ and $t$ sufficiently small.

Completeness. If $M$ is compact and $X$ smooth, there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that every integral curve is defined for $|t|<\varepsilon$ from any starting point: each point has a neighbourhood $U_p$ and a time $\delta_p$, and a finite subcover together with a Lebesgue number gives a uniform existence time for all starting points in one chart neighbourhood. Then for any $T$, composing $\lceil|T|/\varepsilon\rceil$ flow steps defines $\varphi_T$, and uniqueness makes the composition consistent, so $D=\mathbb{R}\times M$: every vector field on a compact manifold is complete. On non-compact manifolds this can fail: for $X=x^2\partial_x$ on $\mathbb{R}$ the integral curve is $$x(t)=\frac{x_0}{1-x_0t}\quad(x_0>0),$$ which blows up as $t\to1/x_0$ and cannot be extended. At a singularity $X(p)=0$ the constant curve is an integral curve, so $\varphi_t(p)=p$ for all $t$; conversely, if $\varphi_t(p)=p$ for all $t$, differentiating at $t=0$ gives $X(p)=0$.

formulas.note: 莱布尼茨法则：光滑向量场与 $C^\infty(M)$ 上的导子（一阶微分算子）一一对应；$X(f)$ 是 $f$ 沿 $X$ 的方向导数。
formulas.noteEn: Leibniz's rule: smooth vector fields correspond one-to-one with derivations (first-order differential operators) of $C^\infty(M)$; $X(f)$ is the directional derivative of $f$ along $X$.

formulas.note: 局部坐标下向量场的表达式与积分曲线的方程：光滑性就是系数 $X^i$ 光滑；积分曲线解一阶 ODE 组。
formulas.noteEn: A vector field in local coordinates and the ODE for its integral curves: smoothness means smooth coefficients $X^i$; integral curves solve a first-order ODE system.

formulas.note: 流的定义与三条基本性质：沿场的方向运动、零时刻不动、半群性质（两边有定义时）；局部存在唯一性来自 ODE 存在唯一性定理。
formulas.noteEn: The definition of the flow and its basic properties: motion along the field, the identity at time zero, and the semigroup law (where both sides are defined); local existence and uniqueness come from the ODE theorem.

formulas.latex: X = -y\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x} + x\,\frac{\partial}{\partial y}:\qquad \varphi_t(x,y) = (x\cos t - y\sin t,\ x\sin t + y\cos t)
formulas.note: 旋转场及其流：积分曲线是以原点为圆心的圆，流对一切 $t \in \mathbb{R}$ 有定义（完备）——即使 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 非紧；原点是奇点。
formulas.noteEn: The rotation field and its flow: integral curves are circles about the origin and the flow is defined for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ (complete) even though $\mathbb{R}^2$ is non-compact; the origin is a singularity.

formulas.latex: X = x^2\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\ \text{on}\ \mathbb{R}:\qquad x(t) = \frac{x_0}{1 - x_0 t}\ \to \infty\ \ (t \to 1/x_0)
formulas.note: 不完备的例子：该积分曲线在有限时间内爆破，无法延拓过 $t = 1/x_0$，故 $X$ 不完备——与「紧流形上必完备」形成对照。
formulas.noteEn: A non-complete example: this integral curve blows up in finite time and cannot be extended past $t = 1/x_0$, so $X$ is incomplete—in contrast with completeness on compact manifolds.

properties: 光滑向量场 $\leftrightarrow$ $C^\infty(M)$ 上满足莱布尼茨法则的实线性算子（导子）一一对应；$X(f)$ 在 $p$ 的值只依赖 $f$ 在 $p$ 附近的值
局部流的存在唯一性来自 ODE 存在唯一性定理：过每点恰有一条极大积分曲线，不同极大积分曲线要么重合、要么像集不交
流性质：$\varphi_0 = \mathrm{id}$、$\varphi_{s+t} = \varphi_s \circ \varphi_t$、$\varphi_t^{-1} = \varphi_{-t}$；$t \mapsto \varphi_t(p)$ 是积分曲线；每个 $\varphi_t$ 是局部微分同胚
**紧流形上任何光滑向量场都完备**（流定义在整个 $\mathbb{R} \times M$ 上）；非紧流形未必：$x^2\,\partial_x$ 在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上不完备，而 $-y\,\partial_x + x\,\partial_y$ 在 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 上完备
奇点：$X(p) = 0 \iff \varphi_t(p) = p$ 对一切 $t$ 成立；此外 $[X,Y] = 0$ 当且仅当两个向量场的流局部交换
propertiesEn: Smooth vector fields correspond one-to-one with real-linear derivations of $C^\infty(M)$ satisfying the Leibniz rule; $X(f)$ at $p$ depends only on $f$ near $p$

Local existence and uniqueness of flows come from the ODE existence and uniqueness theorem: through each point passes exactly one maximal integral curve, and distinct maximal integral curves either coincide or have disjoint images

Flow properties: $\varphi_0 = \mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{s+t} = \varphi_s \circ \varphi_t$, $\varphi_t^{-1} = \varphi_{-t}$; $t \mapsto \varphi_t(p)$ is an integral curve; each $\varphi_t$ is a local diffeomorphism

**Every smooth vector field on a compact manifold is complete** (its flow is defined on all of $\mathbb{R} \times M$); on non-compact manifolds this can fail: $x^2\,\partial_x$ is incomplete on $\mathbb{R}$, while $-y\,\partial_x + x\,\partial_y$ is complete on $\mathbb{R}^2$
Singularities: $X(p) = 0 \iff \varphi_t(p) = p$ for all $t$; moreover $[X,Y] = 0$ if and only if the two flows commute locally

examples.problem: 求旋转向量场 $X = -y\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x} + x\,\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ 在 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 上的流 $\varphi_t$，验证 $\varphi_0 = \mathrm{id}$、半群性质与 $\frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t = X(\varphi_t)$，并说明它的积分曲线与完备性。
examples.solution:
积分曲线满足 $\dot x = -y$、$\dot y = x$，即 $\dot z = iz$（$z = x+iy$），解得
$\varphi_t(x,y) = (x\cos t - y\sin t,\ x\sin t + y\cos t)$。

验证：$\varphi_0(x,y) = (x,y)$，即 $\varphi_0 = \mathrm{id}$；由三角加法公式，$\varphi_s(\varphi_t(x,y)) = \varphi_{s+t}(x,y)$；又
$\frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t(x,y) = (-x\sin t - y\cos t,\ x\cos t - y\sin t)$，而 $X(\varphi_t) = (-(x\sin t + y\cos t),\ x\cos t - y\sin t)$，两者相等。

几何：$|\varphi_t(x,y)|^2 = x^2+y^2$ 保持不变，故积分曲线是以原点为中心的圆（除原点外），$X$ 处处与圆相切；原点处 $X(0) = 0$ 是唯一奇点，流把它固定。

流对一切 $t \in \mathbb{R}$ 都有定义，因此 $X$ 完备——尽管 $\mathbb{R}^2$ 不是紧流形；这印证了「紧 $\Rightarrow$ 完备」但反之不必然。

examples.problem: 说明 $X = x^2\,\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$ 在 $\mathbb{R}$ 上不完备，并解释它与「紧流形上的向量场必完备」不矛盾。
examples.solution:
积分曲线满足 $\dot x = x^2$。分离变量：$\int \frac{dx}{x^2} = \int dt$，得 $-\frac{1}{x} = t - \frac{1}{x_0}$，即
$x(t) = \frac{x_0}{1 - x_0 t}$（$x_0 \neq 0$）。

当 $x_0 > 0$ 时，$x(t) \to +\infty$ 当 $t \to 1/x_0^{-}$：局部解在有限时间内离开任意紧集，无法延拓过 $t = 1/x_0$，因此流只能定义在 $t < 1/x_0$ 上，$X$ 不完备（当 $x_0 < 0$ 时对应 $t > 1/x_0$；$x_0 = 0$ 是奇点，流固定它）。

这不与定理矛盾：定理的前提是**流形紧**，而 $\mathbb{R}$ 非紧；在紧流形上，局部存在时间有一致下界，有限步拼接即可把流延拓到一切 $t \in \mathbb{R}$，故不可能出现这样的有限时间爆破。

expression.text: ẋ = X(x)：积分曲线的 ODE；φ_t 是由 X 生成的流（单参数局部变换群）
expression.note: 记住三条：导子对应、局部流由 ODE 唯一确定、紧流形上向量场完备。
expression.noteEn: Keep three facts: the derivation correspondence, local flows determined uniquely by ODEs, and completeness of every vector field on a compact manifold.

differential-form.definition:
先看一点 $p$。**反对称 $k$ 重线性函数**指 $\lambda: T_pM \times \cdots \times T_pM \to \mathbb{R}$，它对每个变量都线性，而且交换任意两个变量时函数值变号。**$k$ 次微分形式** $\omega$ 就是光滑地给每点 $p$ 指定一个这样的 $\omega_p$（光滑性指在任意局部坐标下分量都是光滑函数）。全体 $k$-形式记作 $\Omega^k(M)$。两个极端情形最重要：**0-形式就是光滑函数**（$\Omega^0(M) = C^\infty(M)$）；**1-形式就是余切向量场**——每点指定一个线性函数 $T_pM \to \mathbb{R}$，是切向量场的对偶对象，最基本的例子是坐标微分 $dx^i$（作用在切向量上就是读出第 $i$ 个坐标分量）。$k$ 重反对称函数构成的空间记作 $\Lambda^k(T_pM)^*$（切空间的 $k$ 次外幂的对偶），它是向量空间，$\dim \Lambda^k(T_pM)^* = \binom{n}{k}$；当 $k > n$ 时 $n$ 维空间里取不出 $k$ 个独立方向，只能得到零。

**外积**把 $k$-形式 $\alpha$ 与 $l$-形式 $\beta$ 乘成 $(k+l)$-形式 $\alpha \wedge \beta$：逐点先乘再交替化，满足双线性、结合律，并在函数乘法下分配。关键性质是**分次交换律**：$\alpha \wedge \beta = (-1)^{kl}\,\beta \wedge \alpha$，其中 $k = |\alpha|$、$l = |\beta|$。特别地对坐标微分，$dx^i \wedge dx^j = -dx^j \wedge dx^i$，于是 $dx^i \wedge dx^i = 0$——「同一个微分的二次方为零」。$n$ 个生成元 $dx^1,\dots,dx^n$ 在外积下张成 $2^n$ 维的外代数，基元素为 $dx^{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^{i_k}$（$i_1 < \cdots < i_k$）。也正因为反对称，一个 $k$-形式总可以只按**递增指标**展开：$\omega = \sum_{i_1 < \cdots < i_k} a_{i_1\cdots i_k}\,dx^{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^{i_k}$，求和只对递增重指标进行，系数 $a_I$ 是任意的光滑函数（独立分量共 $\binom{n}{k}$ 个）。

光滑映射 $f: M \to N$ 把 $N$ 上的形式**拉回**到 $M$：$(f^*\omega)_p(v_1,\dots,v_k) = \omega_{f(p)}\bigl(df_p v_1,\dots,df_p v_k\bigr)$，即用切映射把 $M$ 的方向「送过去」再喂给 $\omega$。拉回与所有结构相容：$f^*(\omega \wedge \eta) = f^*\omega \wedge f^*\eta$，$f^*(d\omega) = d(f^*\omega)$，$(g \circ f)^* = f^* \circ g^*$。尤其注意：**拉回总是有定义，不需要 $f$ 可逆**（方向逆着 $f$）——这是微分形式比向量场好用的原因之一。

**体积形式**是处处非零的 $n$-形式，例如 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 上的 $dx^1 \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^n$：把它作用在 $n$ 个向量上，得到的正是以这 $n$ 个向量为列的矩阵的行列式，这就是「有向体积」的代数化，也是换元积分中雅可比行列式出现的根源。连通 $n$ 维流形**可定向**当且仅当它上面存在处处非零的 $n$-形式。形式让积分脱离坐标：微分形式在流形上可积分，外积自动处理换序的符号，而外微分（下一词条）把经典积分定理统一成一句话。
differential-form.definitionEn:
At a point $p$, an **alternating $k$-linear function** is a map $\lambda: T_pM \times \cdots \times T_pM \to \mathbb{R}$ that is linear in each variable and changes sign when two variables are interchanged. A **differential $k$-form** $\omega$ assigns such an $\omega_p$ to each point smoothly (its components in any local coordinates are smooth functions); the space of $k$-forms is written $\Omega^k(M)$. Two extreme cases matter most: a **0-form is a smooth function** ($\Omega^0(M) = C^\infty(M)$), and a **1-form is a covector field**—a linear functional $T_pM \to \mathbb{R}$ at each point, dual to vector fields, the most basic example being the coordinate differentials $dx^i$ (evaluating them on a tangent vector reads off the $i$-th coordinate component). The alternating $k$-linear functions at $p$ form the space $\Lambda^k(T_pM)^*$ with $\dim \Lambda^k(T_pM)^* = \binom{n}{k}$; for $k > n$ there are no $k$ independent directions and the space is zero.

The **wedge product** multiplies a $k$-form $\alpha$ by an $l$-form $\beta$ into a $(k+l)$-form $\alpha \wedge \beta$: pointwise multiply and alternate; it is bilinear, associative and distributes over sums and function multiplication. The crucial property is **graded commutativity**: $\alpha \wedge \beta = (-1)^{kl}\,\beta \wedge \alpha$ with $k = |\alpha|$, $l = |\beta|$. In particular $dx^i \wedge dx^j = -dx^j \wedge dx^i$ and hence $dx^i \wedge dx^i = 0$—the square of a differential vanishes. The generators $dx^1,\dots,dx^n$ span the $2^n$-dimensional exterior algebra with basis elements $dx^{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^{i_k}$, $i_1 < \cdots < i_k$. Because of antisymmetry every $k$-form can be written with **increasing multi-indices only**: $\omega = \sum_{i_1 < \cdots < i_k} a_{i_1\cdots i_k}\,dx^{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^{i_k}$, with smooth coefficients $a_I$ (there are $\binom{n}{k}$ independent components).

A smooth map $f: M \to N$ **pulls back** forms from $N$ to $M$: $(f^*\omega)_p(v_1,\dots,v_k) = \omega_{f(p)}\bigl(df_p v_1,\dots,df_p v_k\bigr)$, feeding directions from $M$ into $\omega$ via the differential. Pullback is compatible with everything: $f^*(\omega \wedge \eta) = f^*\omega \wedge f^*\eta$, $f^*(d\omega) = d(f^*\omega)$, $(g \circ f)^* = f^* \circ g^*$. In particular pullback is always defined and **does not require $f$ to be invertible** (it goes against the direction of $f$)—one reason forms are more flexible than vector fields.

A **volume form** is an everywhere-nonvanishing $n$-form, e.g. $dx^1 \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^n$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$: evaluated on $n$ vectors it returns the determinant of the matrix with those vectors as columns—the algebra of oriented volume—and it is the source of Jacobian determinants in change-of-variables formulas. A connected $n$-manifold is **orientable** if and only if it carries an everywhere-nonvanishing $n$-form. Forms make integration coordinate-free, the wedge product automatically handles the signs of reordering, and the exterior derivative (next entry) unifies the classical integral theorems into one statement.
derivation: 固定 $p$，令 $V=T_pM$，$\dim V=n$。称 $\omega_p:V^k\to\mathbb{R}$ 为反对称 $k$ 重线性函数，若它对每个变量线性，且交换任意两个变量时变号：$$\omega_p(\dots,v_i,\dots,v_j,\dots)=-\omega_p(\dots,v_j,\dots,v_i,\dots).$$ 等价地，对任意置换 $\sigma\in S_k$ 有 $\omega_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_k)$；特别地，两个变量相等时取值为零。这些函数构成向量空间 $\Lambda^k(T_pM)^*$。$k=0$ 时它就是 $\mathbb{R}$，$k=1$ 时它就是 $T_p^*M$。在整个流形上光滑地指定 $\omega_p$ 即得 $k$-形式，记 $\Omega^k(M)$；光滑指任意图中系数光滑。

取图 $(U,\varphi)$，记 $dx^i$ 为坐标函数 $x^i$ 的微分，$dx^I=dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$（$I=(i_1<\cdots<i_k)$）。每个 $k$-形式在 $U$ 上唯一写成 $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}a_{i_1\cdots i_k}\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k},\\ a_I&=\omega\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_1}},\dots,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_k}}\Bigr).\end{aligned}$$ 唯一性来自基的对偶性：$dx^I(\partial_{j_1},\dots,\partial_{j_k})=\det(\delta^{i_r}_{j_s})$，当 $J=I$ 时为 $1$，当 $J$ 是 $I$ 的置换时为符号，其余为 $0$。指标递增书写避免重复计数，独立分量共 $\binom{n}{k}$ 个；$k>n$ 时 $\binom{n}{k}=0$，只有零形式。$\omega$ 光滑当且仅当所有 $a_I$ 光滑。

外积把 $\alpha\in\Omega^k$ 与 $\beta\in\Omega^l$ 乘为 $k+l$ 形式。采用交替化约定 $$\begin{aligned}&(\alpha\wedge\beta)_p(v_1,\dots,v_{k+l})\\&\quad=\frac{1}{k!\,l!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{k+l}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\\&\qquad\cdot\alpha_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})\,\beta_p(v_{\sigma(k+1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k+l)}).\end{aligned}$$ 它双线性、结合，并满足分次交换律 $$\alpha\wedge\beta=(-1)^{kl}\beta\wedge\alpha.$$ 证明：把前 $k$ 个指标与后 $l$ 个指标整体交换的置换，其符号为 $(-1)^{kl}$，代入定义即把 $\alpha\wedge\beta$ 的求和变成 $\beta\wedge\alpha$ 的求和。推论：$dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$，$dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$；两个 1-形式反交换，而偶数次形式之间交换。注意 1-形式 $\alpha$ 满足 $\alpha\wedge\alpha=0$，但次数为偶的 $\omega$ 未必有 $\omega\wedge\omega=0$（例如 $\mathbb{R}^4$ 上 $\omega=dx^1\wedge dx^2+dx^3\wedge dx^4$ 满足 $\omega\wedge\omega=2\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4\ne0$）。

拉回。设 $F:M\to N$ 光滑，$\omega\in\Omega^k(N)$。定义 $$(F^*\omega)_p(v_1,\dots,v_k):=\omega_{F(p)}\bigl(dF_pv_1,\dots,dF_pv_k\bigr),\qquad v_i\in T_pM.$$ 右边只用到 $F$ 的切映射，故 $F$ 不必可逆；由 $dF_p$ 线性，$F^*\omega$ 仍反对称 $k$ 重线性，光滑性由 $F$ 光滑与链式法则得到。拉回保结构：$$F^*(\omega\wedge\eta)=F^*\omega\wedge F^*\eta,\qquad (G\circ F)^*=F^*\circ G^*.$$ 坐标公式：若 $F$ 由 $y^j=F^j(x)$ 给出，则 $F^*\omega=\sum_I a_I(F(x))\,dF^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dF^{i_k}$；当 $k=n=m$ 时 $$F^*(dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n)=\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n,$$ 雅可比行列式自动出现。

体积形式与定向。由行列式公式 $$dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\det\bigl(v_1,\dots,v_n\bigr)$$（右端是以 $v_j$ 为列的矩阵），该 $n$-形式在基上取 $\pm1$，在退化组上取 $0$。若 $n$-形式 $\Omega$ 处处非零，称它为体积形式；它给出定向：基 $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ 为正，当且仅当 $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$。在坐标中 $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$，$h$ 处处非零；连通流形上两个体积形式相差一个处处非零函数，故恰有两个定向 $\Omega$ 与 $-\Omega$。于是：连通 $n$ 维流形可定向，当且仅当存在处处非零的 $n$-形式；莫比乌斯带不存在这样的形式，故不可定向。

例：$F(r,\theta)=(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$，$r>0$。先算 1-形式拉回：$$F^*dx=\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta,\qquad F^*dy=\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta.$$ 再用 $F^*(\alpha\wedge\beta)=F^*\alpha\wedge F^*\beta$ 与 $dr\wedge dr=d\theta\wedge d\theta=0$：$$\begin{aligned}F^*(dx\wedge dy)&=(\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta)\wedge(\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta)\\&=r\cos^2\theta\,dr\wedge d\theta-r\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\wedge dr\\&=r(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\,dr\wedge d\theta=r\,dr\wedge d\theta.\end{aligned}$$ 这正是面积元 $dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta$，雅可比 $r>0$ 说明该参数化保定向。对比：形式总能拉回（方向与 $F$ 相反），而向量场只有在 $F$ 为微分同胚时才能自然推前；1-形式与向量场的配对由 $\omega(X)=\iota_X\omega$ 给出。
derivationEn: Fix $p$ and put $V=T_pM$, $\dim V=n$. A map $\omega_p:V^k\to\mathbb{R}$ is alternating $k$-linear if it is linear in each variable and changes sign when two variables are interchanged: $$\omega_p(\dots,v_i,\dots,v_j,\dots)=-\omega_p(\dots,v_j,\dots,v_i,\dots).$$ Equivalently $\omega_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_k)$ for every permutation $\sigma\in S_k$; in particular the value is zero when two arguments coincide. These maps form a vector space $\Lambda^k(T_pM)^*$. For $k=0$ it is $\mathbb{R}$, and for $k=1$ it is $T_p^*M$. Assigning $\omega_p$ smoothly over $M$ gives a $k$-form, written $\omega\in\Omega^k(M)$; smooth means smooth coefficients in every chart.

In a chart $(U,\varphi)$ let $dx^i$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^i$ and $dx^I=dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$ for $I=(i_1<\cdots<i_k)$. Every $k$-form on $U$ is uniquely $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n}a_{i_1\cdots i_k}\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k},\\ a_I&=\omega\Bigl(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_1}},\dots,\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i_k}}\Bigr).\end{aligned}$$ Uniqueness comes from duality of the basis: $dx^I(\partial_{j_1},\dots,\partial_{j_k})=\det(\delta^{i_r}_{j_s})$, which is $1$ when $J=I$, the sign of the permutation when $J$ is a permutation of $I$, and $0$ otherwise. Writing indices increasingly avoids double counting, leaving $\binom{n}{k}$ independent components; for $k>n$, $\binom{n}{k}=0$ and only the zero form exists. The form $\omega$ is smooth exactly when all $a_I$ are smooth.

The wedge product multiplies $\alpha\in\Omega^k$ and $\beta\in\Omega^l$ into a $(k+l)$-form. With the alternation convention $$\begin{aligned}&(\alpha\wedge\beta)_p(v_1,\dots,v_{k+l})\\&\quad=\frac{1}{k!\,l!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{k+l}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\\&\qquad\cdot\alpha_p(v_{\sigma(1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k)})\,\beta_p(v_{\sigma(k+1)},\dots,v_{\sigma(k+l)}),\end{aligned}$$ it is bilinear, associative, and satisfies graded commutativity $$\alpha\wedge\beta=(-1)^{kl}\beta\wedge\alpha.$$ Proof: the permutation exchanging the first $k$ and last $l$ indices as blocks has sign $(-1)^{kl}$, and substituting it into the definition turns the sum for $\alpha\wedge\beta$ into the sum for $\beta\wedge\alpha$. Consequences: $dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$ and $dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$; two 1-forms anticommute, while even-degree forms commute. Note that a 1-form $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha\wedge\alpha=0$, but an even-degree $\omega$ need not satisfy $\omega\wedge\omega=0$ (e.g. $\omega=dx^1\wedge dx^2+dx^3\wedge dx^4$ on $\mathbb{R}^4$ has $\omega\wedge\omega=2\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4\ne0$).

Pullback. Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth and $\omega\in\Omega^k(N)$. Define $$(F^*\omega)_p(v_1,\dots,v_k):=\omega_{F(p)}\bigl(dF_pv_1,\dots,dF_pv_k\bigr),\qquad v_i\in T_pM.$$ The right side uses only the differential of $F$, so $F$ need not be invertible; linearity of $dF_p$ makes $F^*\omega$ alternating $k$-linear, and smoothness follows from smoothness of $F$ and the chain rule. Pullback preserves structure: $$F^*(\omega\wedge\eta)=F^*\omega\wedge F^*\eta,\qquad (G\circ F)^*=F^*\circ G^*.$$ In coordinates, if $F$ is given by $y^j=F^j(x)$, then $F^*\omega=\sum_I a_I(F(x))\,dF^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dF^{i_k}$; when $k=n=m$, $$F^*(dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n)=\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial F^j}{\partial x^i}\Bigr)dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n,$$ so the Jacobian determinant appears automatically.

Volume forms and orientation. The determinant formula $$dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\det\bigl(v_1,\dots,v_n\bigr)$$ (the matrix has the $v_j$ as columns) shows that this $n$-form takes the values $\pm1$ on bases and $0$ on degenerate tuples. A nowhere-vanishing $n$-form $\Omega$ is a volume form; it defines an orientation by declaring a basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ positive iff $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$. In coordinates $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ with $h$ nowhere zero; on a connected manifold two volume forms differ by a nowhere-zero function, so there are exactly two orientations $\Omega$ and $-\Omega$. Hence a connected $n$-manifold is orientable if and only if it carries a nowhere-vanishing $n$-form; the Möbius band carries none and is non-orientable.

Example: $F(r,\theta)=(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$ with $r>0$. First pull back the 1-forms: $$F^*dx=\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta,\qquad F^*dy=\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta.$$ Then use $F^*(\alpha\wedge\beta)=F^*\alpha\wedge F^*\beta$ and $dr\wedge dr=d\theta\wedge d\theta=0$: $$\begin{aligned}F^*(dx\wedge dy)&=(\cos\theta\,dr-r\sin\theta\,d\theta)\wedge(\sin\theta\,dr+r\cos\theta\,d\theta)\\&=r\cos^2\theta\,dr\wedge d\theta-r\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\wedge dr\\&=r(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\,dr\wedge d\theta=r\,dr\wedge d\theta.\end{aligned}$$ This is the area element $dx\,dy=r\,dr\,d\theta$, and the Jacobian $r>0$ shows the parametrization is orientation-preserving. Comparison: forms can always be pulled back (against the direction of $F$), whereas vector fields push forward naturally only under diffeomorphisms; a 1-form pairs with a vector field through $\omega(X)=\iota_X\omega$.

formulas.note: 外积的分次交换律（$k = |\alpha|$，$l = |\beta|$）与两个特例：坐标微分反交换，同一个微分的平方为零。
formulas.noteEn: Graded commutativity of the wedge product ($k = |\alpha|$, $l = |\beta|$) and two special cases: coordinate differentials anticommute, and the square of any one of them vanishes.

formulas.note: 形式在局部坐标下的标准写法：求和只遍历递增重指标（因为反对称性）；系数 $a_I$ 为光滑函数，独立分量共 $\binom{n}{k}$ 个。
formulas.noteEn: The standard local expression of a form: the sum runs over increasing multi-indices only (by antisymmetry); the coefficients $a_I$ are smooth, giving $\binom{n}{k}$ independent components.

formulas.note: 点态维数公式：0-形式是函数、1-形式是余切向量；$k > n$ 时没有非零 $k$-形式。
formulas.noteEn: Pointwise dimensions: 0-forms are functions, 1-forms are covectors; there are no nonzero $k$-forms when $k > n$.

formulas.note: 拉回的定义：用切映射把 $M$ 的切向量送进 $N$，再喂给 $\omega$；它总存在，不要求 $f$ 可逆，并与外积、外微分交换。
formulas.noteEn: Pullback: feed tangent vectors of $M$ into $\omega$ through the differential. It always exists, needs no invertibility of $f$, and commutes with the wedge product and the exterior derivative.

formulas.note: 体积形式：作用在 $n$ 个向量上给出有向体积（行列式）；连通流形可定向 $\iff$ 存在处处非零的 $n$-形式。
formulas.noteEn: The volume form returns the oriented volume (a determinant) of $n$ vectors; a connected manifold is orientable if and only if a nowhere-vanishing $n$-form exists.

properties: 反对称性是核心：$dx^i \wedge dx^i = 0$、$dx^i \wedge dx^j = -dx^j \wedge dx^i$；一般地 $\alpha \wedge \beta = (-1)^{|\alpha||\beta|} \beta \wedge \alpha$，两个 1-形式之间反交换，偶数阶之间交换
$k$-形式等价于全反对称的 $(0,k)$-型张量场（指标全反对称，如 $\omega_{ij} = -\omega_{ji}$）：这是把它接入张量分析语言的桥梁
拉回保结构：$f^*(\omega \wedge \eta) = f^*\omega \wedge f^*\eta$ 且 $f^*(d\omega) = d(f^*\omega)$；拉回不需要 $f$ 可逆，而向量场的推前只对微分同胚自然
分量个数：$n$ 维流形上 $k$-形式的独立点态分量有 $\binom{n}{k}$ 个；$k > n$ 时只有零形式
定向与体积：连通 $n$ 维流形可定向 $\iff$ 存在处处非零的 $n$-形式；$\mathbb{R}^n$ 上 $dx^1 \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^n$ 是标准体积形式，作用在正交基上取值为 $\pm 1$
propertiesEn: Antisymmetry is the heart: $dx^i \wedge dx^i = 0$, $dx^i \wedge dx^j = -dx^j \wedge dx^i$, and in general $\alpha \wedge \beta = (-1)^{|\alpha||\beta|} \beta \wedge \alpha$; two 1-forms anticommute, while forms of even degree commute
A $k$-form is the same thing as a totally antisymmetric $(0,k)$-tensor field (components antisymmetric in all indices, e.g. $\omega_{ij} = -\omega_{ji}$)—the bridge to index notation

Pullback preserves structure: $f^*(\omega \wedge \eta) = f^*\omega \wedge f^*\eta$ and $f^*(d\omega) = d(f^*\omega)$; pullback needs no invertibility of $f$, whereas pushing forward vector fields is natural only for diffeomorphisms
Component count: a $k$-form on an $n$-manifold has $\binom{n}{k}$ independent pointwise components; for $k > n$ only the zero form exists

Orientation and volume: a connected $n$-manifold is orientable if and only if it has a nowhere-vanishing $n$-form; on $\mathbb{R}^n$ the form $dx^1 \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^n$ is the standard volume form, taking values $\pm 1$ on orthonormal bases

examples.problem: 计算外积 $(dx + 2\,dy) \wedge (3\,dx - dy)$，并验证分次交换律 $\alpha \wedge \beta = (-1)^{|\alpha||\beta|}\beta \wedge \alpha$ 的一个特例：$(dx \wedge dy) \wedge dz$ 与 $dz \wedge (dx \wedge dy)$ 的关系。
examples.solution:
直接展开：$(dx+2dy) \wedge (3dx-dy) = 3\,dx \wedge dx - dx \wedge dy + 6\,dy \wedge dx - 2\,dy \wedge dy$。

用两条规则：$dx \wedge dx = dy \wedge dy = 0$（同一个微分平方为零），$dy \wedge dx = -dx \wedge dy$（反交换）。于是结果为
$0 - dx \wedge dy - 6\,dx \wedge dy - 0 = -7\,dx \wedge dy$。

交换因子核对：$(3dx-dy) \wedge (dx+2dy) = 3\,dx \wedge dx + 6\,dx \wedge dy - dy \wedge dx - 2\,dy \wedge dy = 7\,dx \wedge dy$，确实等于 $-\bigl[(dx+2dy) \wedge (3dx-dy)\bigr]$，与 $\alpha \wedge \beta = (-1)^{1 \cdot 1}\beta \wedge \alpha$ 一致。

二阶与一阶的情形：$dz \wedge (dx \wedge dy)$，把 $dz$ 移到末尾要跨过 $dx$、$dy$ 两个因子（两次换序，符号 $(-1)^2 = +1$），得 $dz \wedge (dx \wedge dy) = dx \wedge dy \wedge dz = (dx \wedge dy) \wedge dz$，与 $(-1)^{2 \cdot 1} = +1$ 相符。

examples.problem: 设 $f(u,v) = (u\cos v,\ u\sin v)$（极坐标参数化），用拉回计算 $f^*(dx \wedge dy)$，并解释它为什么给出 $dx\,dy = r\,dr\,d\theta$。
examples.solution:
先算 1-形式的拉回（把 $x = u\cos v$、$y = u\sin v$ 代入并取普通微分）：
$f^*dx = d(u\cos v) = \cos v\,du - u\sin v\,dv$，$f^*dy = d(u\sin v) = \sin v\,du + u\cos v\,dv$。

由 $f^*(\omega \wedge \eta) = f^*\omega \wedge f^*\eta$ 与 $du \wedge du = dv \wedge dv = 0$：
$f^*(dx \wedge dy) = (\cos v\,du - u\sin v\,dv) \wedge (\sin v\,du + u\cos v\,dv)$
$= u\cos^2 v\,du \wedge dv - u\sin^2 v\,dv \wedge du = u\cos^2 v\,du \wedge dv + u\sin^2 v\,du \wedge dv = u\,du \wedge dv$。

（中间用 $dv \wedge du = -du \wedge dv$ 把第二项翻号。）把坐标写成习惯记号 $(u,v) = (r,\theta)$，就是 $f^*(dx \wedge dy) = r\,dr \wedge d\theta$，即面积元 $dx\,dy = r\,dr\,d\theta$——雅可比行列式 $r$ 由拉回自动产生，无需求导矩阵再取行列式。

expression.text: ω = Σ_{i₁<…<i_k} a_{i₁…i_k} dx^{i₁} ∧ … ∧ dx^{i_k}（按递增指标书写）
expression.note: k-形式是反对称 k 重线性函数的场；外积反对称、1-形式是余切向量场、0-形式是函数。
expression.noteEn: A k-form is a field of alternating k-linear functions; the wedge is graded-commutative, 1-forms are covector fields and 0-forms are functions.

exterior-derivative.definition:
**外微分** $d$ 是形式上的「求导」算子，$d: \Omega^k(M) \to \Omega^{k+1}(M)$。它由四条性质刻画，而且**满足这四条性质的算子存在且唯一**：
（1）**线性**：$d(\omega + \eta) = d\omega + d\eta$，$d(c\,\omega) = c\,d\omega$（$c$ 为常数）；
（2）**分次莱布尼茨法则**：$d(\omega \wedge \eta) = d\omega \wedge \eta + (-1)^{k}\,\omega \wedge d\eta$，其中 $k = |\omega|$ 是 $\omega$ 的次数——负号只由**左因子 $\omega$** 的次数的奇偶决定，不能丢、不能乱放；
（3）**$d^2 = 0$**：连续作用两次得零；
（4）**对函数就是普通微分**：对 $f \in C^\infty(M)$ 与 $v \in T_pM$，$df_p(v) = v(f)$，坐标下 $df = \sum_i \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^i}\,dx^i$。
性质（2）对 $f \in C^\infty(M)$ 的特例是 $d(f\omega) = df \wedge \omega + f\,d\omega$，说明 $d$ 与乘积的关系像导数（会产生一项 $df \wedge \omega$），而**不是** $C^\infty(M)$-线性算子。在局部坐标下 $d$ 的公式简单到可以当作定义：若 $\omega = \sum_I a_I\,dx^I$（$dx^I = dx^{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge dx^{i_k}$，按递增指标求和），则 $d\omega = \sum_I da_I \wedge dx^I = \sum_{I,j} \frac{\partial a_I}{\partial x^j}\,dx^j \wedge dx^I$：把每个系数当普通函数求微分，再与对应的 $dx^I$ 外积、求和。由此立刻看出 $d^2 = 0$ 的本质：$d(da_I) = \sum_{j,i} \frac{\partial^2 a_I}{\partial x^j \partial x^i}\,dx^j \wedge dx^i$ 中混合偏导 $\frac{\partial^2 a_I}{\partial x^j \partial x^i}$ 关于 $j,i$ 对称，而 $dx^j \wedge dx^i$ 反对称，逐项抵消——这正是「混合偏导数可交换」。

满足 $d\omega = 0$ 的 $\omega$ 叫**闭形式**，能写成 $\omega = d\eta$ 的叫**恰当形式**。由 $d^2 = 0$，**恰当一定闭**；反过来一般**不**成立——「闭而不恰当」的程度完全由流形的拓扑决定，记作 de Rham 上同调 $H^k_{dR}(M) = \bigl\{\text{闭 } k \text{-形式}\bigr\}\big/\bigl\{\text{恰当 } k \text{-形式}\bigr\}$，它精确地刻画流形上有多少个「洞」。最经典的例子是穿孔平面 $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ 上的 $\omega = \frac{-y\,dx + x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}$：可以算出 $d\omega = 0$，但它不是任何整体 $\eta$ 的微分（沿单位圆周的积分 $\oint \omega = 2\pi \neq 0$，而恰当形式沿闭曲线的积分必为零）。**庞加莱引理**给出反向成立的充分条件：在 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 的**星形区域**（更一般地，任何可缩区域）上，每个闭形式都恰当。注意条件与方向：可缩是「没有洞」的精确化，$\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ 绕原点一圈不能收缩，正因如此才出现闭而不恰当的例子。

外微分把经典向量分析一网打尽。在 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 中（欧氏度规＋标准定向）：
• 函数与梯度：由 $df(v) = \langle \nabla f, v \rangle$，梯度就是 $f$ 的「外微分再配上内积」；
• 向量场 $F = (F_1,F_2,F_3)$ 对应 1-形式 $F^{\flat} = F_1\,dx + F_2\,dy + F_3\,dz$，则 $dF^{\flat}$ 的分量正是 $\mathrm{curl}\,F$：$dF^{\flat} = (\partial_y F_3 - \partial_z F_2)\,dy \wedge dz + (\partial_z F_1 - \partial_x F_3)\,dz \wedge dx + (\partial_x F_2 - \partial_y F_1)\,dx \wedge dy$，用 Hodge 星号 $\ast$ 转回 1-形式即 $\ast\,dF^{\flat} = (\mathrm{curl}\,F)^{\flat}$；
• 向量场对应通量 2-形式 $\ast F^{\flat} = F_1\,dy \wedge dz + F_2\,dz \wedge dx + F_3\,dx \wedge dy$，则 $d(\ast F^{\flat}) = (\mathrm{div}\,F)\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$。
于是 $\mathrm{curl} \circ \nabla = 0$ 与 $\mathrm{div} \circ \mathrm{curl} = 0$ 只是 $d^2 = 0$ 的不同化身；格林公式、斯托克斯公式、高斯公式统一为广义斯托克斯定理 $\int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega$。注意这些「翻译」用到了度规与内积（把向量与 1-形式互换、定义 $\ast$、把 $df$ 与 $\nabla f$ 配对），而 $d$ 本身不需要任何度规，它只依赖光滑结构。
derivation: 外微分是满足以下四条的唯一族算子 $d:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{k+1}(M)$：（i）$\mathbb{R}$-线性；（ii）分次莱布尼茨律 $$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^{k}\omega\wedge d\eta,\qquad k=|\omega|;$$（iii）$d^2=0$；（iv）对 $f\in C^\infty(M)$ 与 $v\in T_pM$，$df_p(v)=v(f)$。唯一性：在图中写 $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$，由（ii）与 $d(dx^I)=0$（每个 $dx^I$ 是 1-形式的楔积，而 $d^2x^i=0$）得 $$d\omega=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I,$$ 右边被（i）（iv）完全确定；不同图给出的表达式由转换函数的链式法则一致，故 $d$ 存在且唯一。注意 $d(f\omega)=df\wedge\omega+f\,d\omega$，故 $d$ 不是 $C^\infty(M)$-线性的。

局部公式与低次例子。对 $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$，$$d\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{\partial a_I}{\partial x^j}\,dx^j\wedge dx^I=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I.$$ 0-形式：$df=\sum_i\partial_i f\,dx^i$。1-形式（$n=2$）：设 $\omega=P\,dx+Q\,dy$，则 $$\begin{aligned}d\omega&=dP\wedge dx+dQ\wedge dy\\&=(P_x\,dx+P_y\,dy)\wedge dx+(Q_x\,dx+Q_y\,dy)\wedge dy\\&=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy,\end{aligned}$$ 其中用了 $dx\wedge dx=dy\wedge dy=0$ 与 $dy\wedge dx=-dx\wedge dy$。系数 $Q_x-P_y$ 正是格林公式中的被积函数，也是旋度的 $z$ 分量。结论：$d$ 在坐标中就是「系数求普通微分再外积」。

$d^2=0$。设 $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$，$a_I\in C^2$。连续作用两次：$$d^2\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j,i}\frac{\partial^2 a_I}{\partial x^i\partial x^j}\,dx^i\wedge dx^j\wedge dx^I.$$ 把 $(i,j)$ 与 $(j,i)$ 两项配对：由 Schwarz 定理 $\partial_i\partial_j a_I=\partial_j\partial_i a_I$（系数相同），而 $dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$（符号相反），故两项之和为零；$i=j$ 时 $dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$。于是 $d^2\omega=0$。条件 $a_I\in C^2$ 不可省：证明用到了混合偏导可交换。结论：$d^2=0$ 在坐标中就是「二阶偏导对称、外积反对称」这两件事的相容性，它使 $\{\Omega^k(M),d\}$ 成为上链复形。

分次莱布尼茨律的符号。只需对单项式 $\omega=f\,dx^I$、$\eta=g\,dx^J$ 验证，$k=|I|$、$l=|J|$，再用双线性推广。由 $d(dx^I)=0$ 与普通乘积法则：$$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d(fg\,dx^I\wedge dx^J)=(g\,df+f\,dg)\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J.$$ 第一项就是 $d\omega\wedge\eta$；第二项中 $dg$ 是 1-形式，把它从 $dx^I$ 的右边移到左边要跨过 $k$ 个 1-形式，每次换序变号，故 $$f\,dg\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k f\,dx^I\wedge dg\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta.$$ 相加即得 $d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta$。结论：符号只由左因子次数 $k$ 决定，不能写成 $(-1)^l$ 或省略；$k$ 为偶数时两项同号相加，为奇数时第二项反号。

闭形式与恰当形式。称 $\omega$ 闭若 $d\omega=0$，恰当若 $\omega=d\eta$。由 $d^2=0$，恰当必闭：$d\omega=d^2\eta=0$。反向一般不成立。例：在 $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ 上 $$\omega=\frac{-y\,dx+x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}=P\,dx+Q\,dy,$$ 直接求导得 $$Q_x=\frac{(x^2+y^2)-2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}=\frac{y^2-x^2}{r^4}=P_y,$$ 故 $d\omega=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy=0$，$\omega$ 闭。但若 $\omega=d\eta$，沿单位圆 $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ 有 $\oint_\gamma\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}dt=2\pi$，而恰当形式沿闭曲线积分必为 $\eta(\gamma(2\pi))-\eta(\gamma(0))=0$，矛盾，故 $\omega$ 不恰当。

庞加莱引理与其条件。设 $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ 关于某点星形（特别地 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 本身或凸域），$\omega\in\Omega^k(U)$ 闭，$k\ge1$。定义同伦算子 $$(K\omega)_x(v_1,\dots,v_{k-1})=\int_0^1 t^{k-1}\,\omega_{tx}\bigl(x,v_1,\dots,v_{k-1}\bigr)\,dt,$$ 直接计算可得链同伦公式 $$d(K\omega)+K(d\omega)=\omega,\qquad k\ge1.$$ 于是 $d\omega=0$ 时 $\omega=d(K\omega)$：每个闭形式都恰当。条件「星形/可缩」不可省：$\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ 不星形，第 5 步的 $\omega$ 闭而不恰当；$H^1_{dR}(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\})\cong\mathbb{R}$ 正度量了这个「洞」。最后，$d$ 与拉回交换：$F^*(d\omega)=d(F^*\omega)$（坐标中两边都等于对 $a_I\circ F$ 求偏导再外积），故 $d$ 是光滑流形范畴内的自然算子；在 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 中配合度规与 Hodge 星号，$d$ 沿 $0\to1\to2\to3$ 形式链分别对应梯度、旋度、散度，$d^2=0$ 对应 $\operatorname{curl}\nabla=0$ 与 $\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}=0$。
derivationEn: The exterior derivative is the unique family of operators $d:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{k+1}(M)$ satisfying: (i) $\mathbb{R}$-linearity; (ii) the graded Leibniz rule $$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^{k}\omega\wedge d\eta,\qquad k=|\omega|;$$ (iii) $d^2=0$; (iv) $df_p(v)=v(f)$ for $f\in C^\infty(M)$ and $v\in T_pM$. Uniqueness: write $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$ in a chart. By (ii) and $d(dx^I)=0$ (each $dx^I$ is a wedge of 1-forms and $d^2x^i=0$), $$d\omega=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I,$$ whose right side is completely determined by (i) and (iv); expressions from different charts agree by the chain rule for transition maps, so $d$ exists and is unique. Note $d(f\omega)=df\wedge\omega+f\,d\omega$, so $d$ is not $C^\infty(M)$-linear.

Local formula and low-degree examples. For $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$, $$d\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{\partial a_I}{\partial x^j}\,dx^j\wedge dx^I=\sum_I da_I\wedge dx^I.$$ For a 0-form, $df=\sum_i\partial_i f\,dx^i$. For a 1-form in $n=2$, write $\omega=P\,dx+Q\,dy$; then $$\begin{aligned}d\omega&=dP\wedge dx+dQ\wedge dy\\&=(P_x\,dx+P_y\,dy)\wedge dx+(Q_x\,dx+Q_y\,dy)\wedge dy\\&=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy,\end{aligned}$$ using $dx\wedge dx=dy\wedge dy=0$ and $dy\wedge dx=-dx\wedge dy$. The coefficient $Q_x-P_y$ is exactly the integrand in Green's theorem and the $z$-component of the curl. Thus in coordinates $d$ differentiates the coefficients and wedges.

$d^2=0$. Let $\omega=\sum_I a_I dx^I$ with $a_I\in C^2$. Applying $d$ twice, $$d^2\omega=\sum_I\sum_{j,i}\frac{\partial^2 a_I}{\partial x^i\partial x^j}\,dx^i\wedge dx^j\wedge dx^I.$$ Pair the terms $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$: Schwarz's theorem gives equal coefficients $\partial_i\partial_j a_I=\partial_j\partial_i a_I$, while $dx^i\wedge dx^j=-dx^j\wedge dx^i$ gives opposite signs, so each pair cancels; for $i=j$, $dx^i\wedge dx^i=0$. Hence $d^2\omega=0$. The hypothesis $a_I\in C^2$ cannot be dropped, since the proof uses equality of mixed partials. Thus $d^2=0$ is precisely the compatibility of symmetric second partials with the antisymmetric wedge, and it makes $\{\Omega^k(M),d\}$ a cochain complex.

The sign in the graded Leibniz rule. It suffices to check monomials $\omega=f\,dx^I$, $\eta=g\,dx^J$ with $k=|I|$, $l=|J|$, then extend by bilinearity. Using $d(dx^I)=0$ and the ordinary product rule, $$d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d(fg\,dx^I\wedge dx^J)=(g\,df+f\,dg)\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J.$$ The first term is $d\omega\wedge\eta$. In the second, $dg$ is a 1-form; moving it from the right of $dx^I$ to the left crosses $k$ one-forms, each crossing changing the sign, so $$f\,dg\wedge dx^I\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k f\,dx^I\wedge dg\wedge dx^J=(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta.$$ Adding gives $d(\omega\wedge\eta)=d\omega\wedge\eta+(-1)^k\omega\wedge d\eta$. Hence the sign is fixed by the degree $k$ of the left factor and may not be replaced by $(-1)^l$ or omitted; for even $k$ the two terms add with the same sign, for odd $k$ the second is reversed.

Closed and exact forms. A form is closed if $d\omega=0$ and exact if $\omega=d\eta$. Since $d^2=0$, exact implies closed: $d\omega=d^2\eta=0$. The converse fails in general. Example: on $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$, $$\omega=\frac{-y\,dx+x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}=P\,dx+Q\,dy,$$ and direct differentiation gives $$Q_x=\frac{(x^2+y^2)-2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}=\frac{y^2-x^2}{r^4}=P_y,$$ so $d\omega=(Q_x-P_y)\,dx\wedge dy=0$ and $\omega$ is closed. But if $\omega=d\eta$, then along the unit circle $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t)$ one has $\oint_\gamma\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}dt=2\pi$, whereas an exact form integrates to $\eta(\gamma(2\pi))-\eta(\gamma(0))=0$ over a closed curve—a contradiction, so $\omega$ is not exact.

The Poincaré lemma and its hypothesis. Let $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be star-shaped with respect to some point (in particular $\mathbb{R}^n$ itself or a convex domain), and let $\omega\in\Omega^k(U)$ be closed with $k\ge1$. Define the homotopy operator $$(K\omega)_x(v_1,\dots,v_{k-1})=\int_0^1 t^{k-1}\,\omega_{tx}\bigl(x,v_1,\dots,v_{k-1}\bigr)\,dt.$$ A direct computation gives the chain-homotopy identity $$d(K\omega)+K(d\omega)=\omega,\qquad k\ge1.$$ Hence if $d\omega=0$, then $\omega=d(K\omega)$: every closed form is exact. The star-shaped (or contractible) hypothesis is essential: $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ is not star-shaped, and the form of Step 5 is closed but not exact; $H^1_{dR}(\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\})\cong\mathbb{R}$ measures exactly this hole. Finally, $d$ commutes with pullback: $F^*(d\omega)=d(F^*\omega)$ (in coordinates both sides differentiate $a_I\circ F$ and wedge), so $d$ is a natural operator of smooth manifolds; on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a metric and the Hodge star, $d$ encodes gradient, curl and divergence along the chain of $0$-, $1$-, $2$-, $3$-forms, and $d^2=0$ becomes $\operatorname{curl}\nabla=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}=0$.

formulas.note: 分次莱布尼茨法则与 $d^2 = 0$：符号 $(-1)^{|\omega|}$ 由左因子 $\omega$ 的次数决定；这两条加上线性与「函数上为普通微分」唯一确定 $d$。
formulas.noteEn: The graded Leibniz rule and $d^2 = 0$: the sign $(-1)^{|\omega|}$ is fixed by the degree of the left factor; these two, together with linearity and agreement with $df$ on functions, determine $d$ uniquely.

formulas.latex: \omega = \sum_I a_I\,dx^I\ \Longrightarrow\ d\omega = \sum_I da_I \wedge dx^I = \sum_{I,j} \frac{\partial a_I}{\partial x^j}\,dx^j \wedge dx^I
formulas.note: 局部坐标公式：系数逐个求普通微分再外积；$d^2 = 0$ 在此化为「混合偏导可交换（对称）与 $dx^j \wedge dx^i$ 反对称相抵消」。
formulas.noteEn: The local formula: differentiate each coefficient and wedge. Here $d^2 = 0$ becomes the cancellation between symmetric mixed partials and the antisymmetric $dx^j \wedge dx^i$.

formulas.latex: \omega = P\,dx + Q\,dy\ \Longrightarrow\ d\omega = \Bigl(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\Bigr) dx \wedge dy
formulas.note: 二维 1-形式的外微分：系数 $Q_x - P_y$ 恰好是旋度的 $z$ 分量，与格林公式 $\oint_{\partial D} (P\,dx+Q\,dy) = \iint_D (Q_x - P_y)\,dx\,dy$ 的被积函数一致。
formulas.noteEn: The exterior derivative of a planar 1-form: the coefficient $Q_x - P_y$ is exactly the $z$-component of the curl and is the integrand in Green's theorem.

formulas.latex: df \ \leftrightarrow\ \nabla f,\qquad \ast\, d(F^{\flat}) = (\mathrm{curl}\,F)^{\flat},\qquad d(\ast F^{\flat}) = (\mathrm{div}\,F)\, dx \wedge dy \wedge dz
formulas.note: 与梯度、旋度、散度的对应：用度规把向量与 1-形式互换、用 Hodge 星号 $\ast$ 在 1-形式与 2-形式间转换；$d$ 本身不需要度规。
formulas.noteEn: Correspondence with gradient, curl and divergence: the metric identifies vectors with 1-forms and the Hodge star converts between 1- and 2-forms; $d$ itself needs no metric.

formulas.latex: \oint_{\partial D} \bigl(P\,dx + Q\,dy\bigr) = \iint_D \Bigl(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\Bigr) dx\,dy,\qquad \int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega
formulas.note: 格林公式（广义斯托克斯定理在平面上的特例）与一般形式：后者是流形上的「牛顿–莱布尼茨公式」，把闭形式与恰当形式、边界与内部连接起来。
formulas.noteEn: Green's theorem (a planar case of generalized Stokes) and the general form: the latter is the fundamental theorem of calculus on manifolds, linking boundary and interior.

properties: 唯一性：满足四条性质（线性、分次莱布尼茨、$d^2 = 0$、函数上为普通微分）的外微分存在且唯一；坐标公式 $d\omega = \sum_I da_I \wedge dx^I$ 自动满足它们
与拉回交换：$f^*(d\omega) = d(f^*\omega)$；但 $d$ 不是 $C^\infty$-线性的，而有乘积律 $d(f\omega) = df \wedge \omega + f\,d\omega$
恰当 $\Rightarrow$ 闭（因为 $d^2 = 0$）；反之取决于拓扑。庞加莱引理：$\mathbb{R}^n$ 或任何星形（可缩）区域上闭 $\Rightarrow$ 恰当；$\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ 上的 $\frac{-y\,dx+x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}$ 闭而不恰当

二维：$d(P\,dx+Q\,dy) = (Q_x - P_y)\,dx \wedge dy$ 与旋度的 $z$ 分量一致；三维：$\nabla$、$\mathrm{curl}$、$\mathrm{div}$ 是「函数 → 1-形式 → 2-形式 → 3-形式」链上 $d$ 与 $\ast$ 的组合，$\mathrm{curl} \circ \nabla = 0$、$\mathrm{div} \circ \mathrm{curl} = 0$ 都是 $d^2 = 0$
广义斯托克斯定理 $\int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega$（$M$ 紧定向带边、$\omega$ 为 $(n-1)$-形式）统一了格林、斯托克斯、高斯公式与微积分基本定理；Cartan 公式 $L_X = d\,\iota_X + \iota_X\,d$ 把 $d$ 与李导数、内乘联系起来
propertiesEn: Uniqueness: an exterior derivative satisfying the four properties (linearity, graded Leibniz, $d^2 = 0$, agreement with $df$ on functions) exists and is unique; the local formula $d\omega = \sum_I da_I \wedge dx^I$ satisfies them automatically
It commutes with pullback: $f^*(d\omega) = d(f^*\omega)$; it is not $C^\infty$-linear but obeys the product rule $d(f\omega) = df \wedge \omega + f\,d\omega$

Exact $\Rightarrow$ closed (since $d^2 = 0$); the converse depends on topology. Poincaré lemma: on $\mathbb{R}^n$ or any star-shaped (contractible) domain, closed $\Rightarrow$ exact; $\frac{-y\,dx+x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}$ on $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ is closed but not exact

In dimension two $d(P\,dx+Q\,dy) = (Q_x - P_y)\,dx \wedge dy$ matches the $z$-component of the curl; in dimension three, $\nabla$, $\mathrm{curl}$ and $\mathrm{div}$ arise from $d$ and $\ast$ along the chain functions → 1-forms → 2-forms → 3-forms, and both $\mathrm{curl} \circ \nabla = 0$ and $\mathrm{div} \circ \mathrm{curl} = 0$ are $d^2 = 0$

The generalized Stokes theorem $\int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega$ (for compact oriented $M$ with boundary and an $(n-1)$-form $\omega$) unifies Green, Stokes, Gauss and the fundamental theorem of calculus; the Cartan formula $L_X = d\,\iota_X + \iota_X\,d$ links $d$ to Lie derivatives and interior products

examples.problem: 在 $\mathbb{R}^3$ 中验证分次莱布尼茨法则：取 $\omega = x\,dy$（1 次）与 $\eta = z\,dx$（1 次），计算 $d(\omega \wedge \eta)$ 与 $d\omega \wedge \eta + (-1)^{|\omega|}\,\omega \wedge d\eta$，并说明符号的必要性；再取 $|\omega| = 2$ 的形式做一次对照。
examples.solution:
左端：$\omega \wedge \eta = x\,dy \wedge z\,dx = xz\,dy \wedge dx = -xz\,dx \wedge dy$，于是
$d(\omega \wedge \eta) = -d(xz) \wedge dx \wedge dy = -(z\,dx + x\,dz) \wedge dx \wedge dy = -x\,dz \wedge dx \wedge dy = -x\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$，其中用了 $dx \wedge dx = 0$ 与 $dz \wedge dx \wedge dy = dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$（两次换序）。

右端：$d\omega = dx \wedge dy$，$d\eta = dz \wedge dx$，于是
$d\omega \wedge \eta = (dx \wedge dy) \wedge (z\,dx) = z\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dx = 0$（$dx$ 出现两次），
$(-1)^{|\omega|}\,\omega \wedge d\eta = (-1)^1 (x\,dy) \wedge (dz \wedge dx) = -x\,dy \wedge dz \wedge dx = -x\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$。
两端相等，都是 $-x\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$。若把符号误写成 $+1$，右端将得到 $+x\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$，与左端差一个负号——这就是 $(-1)^{|\omega|}$ 的作用。

$|\omega| = 2$ 的对照：取 $\theta = x^2\,dy \wedge dz$、$h = e^x$（0 次）。左端 $d(\theta \wedge h) = d(x^2e^x\,dy \wedge dz) = (2x+x^2)e^x\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$；右端 $d\theta \wedge h + (-1)^2\,\theta \wedge dh = 2xe^x\,dx \wedge dy \wedge dz + x^2e^x\,dy \wedge dz \wedge dx$，而 $dy \wedge dz \wedge dx = dx \wedge dy \wedge dz$，两项相加与左端一致——偶数次时符号为 $+1$，也确实应取 $+1$。

examples.problem: 证明 $\omega = \frac{-y\,dx + x\,dy}{x^2+y^2}$ 在 $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ 上闭但不恰当，并说明这与庞加莱引理不矛盾。
examples.solution:
闭：记 $r^2 = x^2+y^2$，$P = \frac{-y}{r^2}$，$Q = \frac{x}{r^2}$。计算偏导
$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = \frac{r^2 - x \cdot 2x}{r^4} = \frac{y^2 - x^2}{r^4}$，$\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = \frac{-r^2 + y \cdot 2y}{r^4} = \frac{y^2 - x^2}{r^4}$，
两者相等，故 $d\omega = (Q_x - P_y)\,dx \wedge dy = 0$，即 $\omega$ 闭。

不恰当：若在整个 $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ 上 $\omega = d\eta$，取单位圆 $\gamma(t) = (\cos t, \sin t)$，$t \in [0, 2\pi]$。沿圆有 $r^2 = 1$，$dx = -\sin t\,dt$，$dy = \cos t\,dt$，于是
$\oint_{\gamma}\omega = \int_0^{2\pi}\bigl[(-\sin t)(-\sin t) + (\cos t)(\cos t)\bigr]dt = \int_0^{2\pi} dt = 2\pi$。
但恰当形式沿闭曲线的积分必为零：$\oint_{\gamma} d\eta = \int_0^{2\pi}\frac{d}{dt}\eta(\gamma(t))\,dt = \eta(\gamma(2\pi)) - \eta(\gamma(0)) = 0$（链式法则＋微积分基本定理，不需要 $\eta$ 有任何整体性假设，只要它定义在含 $\gamma$ 的区域上）。矛盾，故 $\omega$ 不恰当。

与庞加莱引理不矛盾：$\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ 不是星形、也不是可缩区域（绕原点一整圈无法缩成一点）。$\omega$ 局部上等于 $d\theta$（$\theta$ 为极角），但极角不能在整个穿孔平面上定义为单值光滑函数，所以没有整体原函数；在 $\mathbb{R}^2$（或任何星形区域）上引理保证闭形式必恰当。

expression.text: d : Ω^k(M) → Ω^{k+1}(M)，且 d² = 0；分次莱布尼茨律的符号为 (−1)^{|ω|}
expression.note: 外微分由四条性质唯一确定：线性、分次莱布尼茨、d² = 0、函数上为普通微分。
expression.noteEn: The exterior derivative is determined by four properties: linearity, graded Leibniz, d² = 0, and the ordinary differential on functions.

manifold-integration.definition:
把一元与多元积分搬上流形，最顺手的载体是**微分形式**。设 $M$ 是 $n$ 维**可定向**流形，$\omega$ 是 $M$ 上的 $n$-形式（顶次形式）。在局部坐标 $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ 中 $\omega$ 唯一地写成
$$\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n,$$
于是它在坐标卡 $U$（参数化 $x=\varphi(p)$）上的积分就定义为系数函数的普通多重积分
$$\int_U\omega=\int_{\varphi(U)}f(x)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n.$$
再取从属于坐标覆盖的单位分解 $\{\rho_i\}$，令 $\int_M\omega=\sum_i\int_{U_i}\rho_i\,\omega$，就得到与坐标卡选择无关的整体积分。

为什么非要**定向**？因为换坐标 $y=\psi(x)$ 时，形式的系数按**带符号**的雅可比行列式变换：
$$dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n=\det\left(\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}\right)dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n.$$
普通多重积分换元取绝对值 $|\det|$，形式积分却必须保留符号——$\omega$ 自带方向信息。要让各坐标卡的积分互相兼容，就要求一切转换函数的雅可比行列式恒正，这正是**定向**；等价的描述是：存在一张**处处非零的 $n$-形式**（体积形式）$\Omega$，约定它代表正体积。连通可定向流形恰有两个定向、互为反向；翻转定向，积分整体变号：$\int_{-M}\omega=-\int_M\omega$。

反面典型是**莫比乌斯带**：沿中线走一圈，横向切向量回来时已经反向（粘合处的微分为 $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$），无法连续地选出一致的定向，因此它不可定向、没有体积形式，$\int_M\omega$ 对 2-形式无从谈起。球面、环面、一切李群都可定向。可见「顶次形式能不能整体积分」不是技术细节，而是流形整体拓扑的性质。

积分还统一了熟悉的公式：平面上区域 $D$ 上的 $f\,dx\wedge dy$ 的积分就是二重积分；$\mathbb R^3$ 中曲面上把体积形式沿场 $F$ 内乘收缩成通量形式 $\iota_F(dx\wedge dy\wedge dz)=F_1\,dy\wedge dz+F_2\,dz\wedge dx+F_3\,dx\wedge dy$，它的积分就是通量 $\iint F\cdot dS$。并且积分是保定向微分同胚的不变量：$\int_N\Phi^*\omega=\int_M\omega$——这正是微积分换元公式在流形上的样子。
manifold-integration.definitionEn:
The natural vehicle for moving one-variable and multivariable integration onto manifolds is the **differential form**. Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional **orientable** manifold and let $\omega$ be an $n$-form (a top-degree form) on it. In local coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ it can be written uniquely as
$$\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n,$$
and its integral over the chart $U$ (parametrised by $x=\varphi(p)$) is defined to be the ordinary multiple integral of the coefficient,
$$\int_U\omega=\int_{\varphi(U)}f(x)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n.$$
Choosing a partition of unity $\{\rho_i\}$ subordinate to a coordinate cover and setting $\int_M\omega=\sum_i\int_{U_i}\rho_i\,\omega$ gives a global integral independent of the charts.

Why is an **orientation** indispensable? Because under a change of coordinates $y=\psi(x)$ the coefficient of a form transforms by the **signed** Jacobian:
$$dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n=\det\left(\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}\right)dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n.$$
Ordinary multiple integrals use $|\det|$ in the substitution rule, whereas form integrals keep the sign, because a form already carries orientation data. For the integrals computed in different charts to agree, every transition function must have positive Jacobian determinant — that is precisely an **orientation**; equivalently, an orientation is a **nowhere-vanishing $n$-form** (a volume form) $\Omega$ declared positive. A connected orientable manifold has exactly two orientations, opposite to each other; reversing the orientation flips the sign of the integral: $\int_{-M}\omega=-\int_M\omega$.

The standard counterexample is the **Möbius band**: walking once around the central circle brings a transverse tangent vector back reversed (the gluing differential is $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$), so no consistent choice of directions exists; the band is non-orientable, carries no volume form, and $\int_M\omega$ for a 2-form is meaningless. Spheres, tori and all Lie groups are orientable. Whether a top-degree form can be integrated globally is thus a property of the global topology of the manifold, not a technicality.

The integral also unifies familiar constructions: on a plane region $D$, integrating $f\,dx\wedge dy$ is just the double integral; on a surface in $\mathbb R^3$, contracting the volume form with a field $F$ gives the flux form $\iota_F(dx\wedge dy\wedge dz)=F_1\,dy\wedge dz+F_2\,dz\wedge dx+F_3\,dx\wedge dy$, whose integral is the flux $\iint F\cdot dS$. Finally, the integral is invariant under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms: $\int_N\Phi^*\omega=\int_M\omega$ — the change-of-variables formula in its manifold form.
derivation: 定向。设 $M$ 是 $n$ 维光滑流形。一个定向可由图册给出：要求所有转换函数满足 $$\det D\bigl(\varphi_\beta\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}\bigr)(x)>0$$ 在重叠区恒成立。等价地，定向由处处非零的 $n$-形式（体积形式）$\Omega$ 给出：把满足 $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$ 的基定为正基。两者等价：给定 $\Omega$，在图中写 $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$，$h\ne0$，只取 $h>0$ 的图，则转换函数的雅可比等于 $h_\alpha/h_\beta>0$；反之给定正雅可比图册，用单位分解把各图的 $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ 乘以非负系数拼成整体 $\Omega$。连通可定向流形恰有两个定向。莫比乌斯带两者都不满足，故不可定向。

局部积分。设 $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$ 的支撑含于一张定向坐标卡 $(U,\varphi)$，在图中 $$\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\qquad\bigl(f\in C_c(\varphi(U))\bigr),$$ 其中 $f$ 连续且紧支撑（更一般地，只要求 $f$ 可积）。定义 $$\int_M\omega:=\int_{\varphi(U)}f(x^1,\dots,x^n)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n,$$ 右端是普通的 $n$ 重（黎曼或勒贝格）积分。这是定义，不是定理；它把形式的积分化为系数函数的积分。条件：$f$ 可积（连续且紧支撑时自动可积），$\omega$ 是顶次形式——低于 $n$ 次的形式在 $n$ 维流形上没有这种积分。

与坐标卡无关。设另一张定向卡 $(V,\psi)$，$y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$，在重叠区 $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\\&=f\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr)dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n\\&=:\tilde f\,dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ 普通换元公式给出 $$\begin{aligned}&\int f(x)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n\\&\quad=\int f\bigl(x(y)\bigr)\Bigl|\det\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr|\,dy^1\cdots dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ 两张卡定向相容，故 $\det(\partial x/\partial y)=\det D(\varphi\circ\psi^{-1})>0$，绝对值可以去掉，右端恰是 $\int\tilde f\,dy$。结论：局部积分在重叠区一致；定向的唯一作用就是让雅可比的正负号与形式自带的符号相匹配，从而不需要绝对值。

整体积分。取局部有限定向图册 $\{(U_i,\varphi_i)\}$ 与从属的单位分解 $\{\rho_i\}$：$\rho_i\in C_c^\infty(U_i)$，$0\le\rho_i\le1$，$\sum_i\rho_i=1$（每点附近只有有限项非零）。对紧支撑的 $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$，定义 $$\int_M\omega:=\sum_i\int_{U_i}\rho_i\,\omega.$$ 每一项的支撑紧含于 $U_i$，由第 2 步有定义；局部有限性使和式中每点只有有限项非零，故求和有意义。与选择无关：若 $\{\sigma_j\}$ 是另一组单位分解，则 $$\sum_i\int\rho_i\omega=\sum_i\sum_j\int\rho_i\sigma_j\omega=\sum_j\int\sigma_j\omega,$$ 中间交换求和由局部有限性保证，且 $\sum_i\rho_i=\sum_j\sigma_j=1$。结论：$\int_M$ 是 $\Omega^n_c(M)$ 上的线性泛函；若 $M$ 不紧，则需 $\omega$ 紧支撑（或绝对可积）才能保证收敛。

边界定向与 Stokes。设 $M$ 紧、可定向、带光滑边界，$\dim M=n$。在 $p\in\partial M$ 处有直和 $T_pM=T_p\partial M\oplus\mathbb{R}
u$，$
u$ 为外法向。约定：$\partial M$ 的基 $(e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})$ 为正，当且仅当 $(
u,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})$ 是 $T_pM$ 的正基（「外法向优先」）。模型情形 $\mathbb{H}^n=\{x_n\ge0\}$、标准定向 $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$：外法向 $
u=-\partial_n$，而 $$\det(-\partial_n,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1})=(-1)^n\det(e_1,\dots,e_{n-1},e_n),$$ 故 $\partial\mathbb{H}^n=\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ 的诱导定向是标准定向乘以 $(-1)^n$。在此约定下 Stokes 公式为 $$\int_M d\omega=\int_{\partial M}\omega,\qquad \omega\in\Omega^{n-1}(M),$$ 且 $M$ 紧、$\partial M$ 光滑、$\omega$ 为 $C^1$（$M$ 不紧时要求 $\omega$ 紧支撑）。符号检验：取 $\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{n-1}$，则 $d\omega=(-1)^{n-1}\partial_nf\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$，故 $\int_Md\omega=(-1)^{n-1}\int_{\mathbb{H}^n}\partial_nf=(-1)^n\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n-1}}f(x,0)\,dx$，与上面诱导定向给出的 $\int_{\partial M}\omega$ 一致。

例与不可定向情形。单位圆盘 $D=\{x^2+y^2\le1\}$ 取标准定向 $dx\wedge dy$，$\omega=x\,dy$，$d\omega=dx\wedge dy$。则 $$\int_Dd\omega=\operatorname{area}(D)=\pi,\qquad \int_{\partial D}\omega=\int_0^{2\pi}\cos^2t\,dt=\pi,$$ 边界取逆时针（外法向优先在 $D$ 上确为逆时针），Stokes 成立。再如 $S^2$ 取外法向，$\omega=x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy$，$d\omega=3\,dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$，故 $\int_{S^2}\omega=\int_{B^3}3\,dV=4\pi$，等于 $S^2$ 的面积；把参数化次序颠倒则得 $-4\pi$。若 $M$ 不可定向（莫比乌斯带），顶次形式无法整体积分，但仍可积分密度 $|\omega|$（如面积元 $\sqrt{EG-F^2}\,du\,dv$）；Stokes 在链上使用时不要求 $M$ 整体可定向。
derivationEn: Orientation. Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold. An orientation can be given by an atlas whose transition maps satisfy $$\det D\bigl(\varphi_\beta\circ\varphi_\alpha^{-1}\bigr)(x)>0$$ on every overlap. Equivalently, an orientation is given by a nowhere-vanishing $n$-form (volume form) $\Omega$: declare a basis positive when $\Omega_p(v_1,\dots,v_n)>0$. The two descriptions agree: given $\Omega$, write $\Omega=h\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ in a chart with $h\ne0$ and keep only charts with $h>0$; then the transition Jacobian equals $h_\alpha/h_\beta>0$. Conversely, given a positive-Jacobian atlas, a partition of unity combines the local $dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n$ with nonnegative coefficients into a global $\Omega$. A connected orientable manifold has exactly two orientations. The Möbius band admits neither, hence is non-orientable.

Local integral. Let $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$ have support inside an oriented chart $(U,\varphi)$, where $$\omega=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\qquad\bigl(f\in C_c(\varphi(U))\bigr),$$ with $f$ continuous and compactly supported (more generally, $f$ integrable). Define $$\int_M\omega:=\int_{\varphi(U)}f(x^1,\dots,x^n)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n,$$ the ordinary $n$-fold (Riemann or Lebesgue) integral on the right. This is a definition, not a theorem; it reduces the integral of a form to the integral of its coefficient. Hypotheses: $f$ integrable (automatic for continuous compactly supported $f$), and $\omega$ of top degree—forms of degree below $n$ have no such integral on an $n$-manifold.

Chart independence. Let $(V,\psi)$ be another oriented chart and $y=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}(x)$. On the overlap, $$\begin{aligned}\omega&=f\,dx^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^n\\&=f\det\Bigl(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr)dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n\\&=:\tilde f\,dy^1\wedge\cdots\wedge dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ The substitution formula gives $$\begin{aligned}&\int f(x)\,dx^1\cdots dx^n\\&\quad=\int f\bigl(x(y)\bigr)\Bigl|\det\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\Bigr|\,dy^1\cdots dy^n.\end{aligned}$$ The charts are compatibly oriented, so $\det(\partial x/\partial y)=\det D(\varphi\circ\psi^{-1})>0$ and the absolute value can be dropped; the right side is exactly $\int\tilde f\,dy$. Hence the local integrals agree on overlaps; the sole role of the orientation is to match the sign of the Jacobian with the sign carried by the form, making the absolute value unnecessary.

Global integral. Choose a locally finite oriented atlas $\{(U_i,\varphi_i)\}$ and a subordinate partition of unity $\{\rho_i\}$: $\rho_i\in C_c^\infty(U_i)$, $0\le\rho_i\le1$, $\sum_i\rho_i=1$ (only finitely many terms are nonzero near each point). For compactly supported $\omega\in\Omega^n(M)$ define $$\int_M\omega:=\sum_i\int_{U_i}\rho_i\,\omega.$$ Each term has support compactly contained in $U_i$ and is defined by Step 2; local finiteness makes the sum finite near each point, so it is meaningful.
